```sql
ALTER TABLE "supplier_payments" ADD CONSTRAINT "supplier_payments_amount_check" CHECK ("supplier_payments"."amount" > 0 AND "supplier_payments"."applied" >= 0 AND "supplier_payments"."refunded" >= 0 AND "supplier_payments"."applied" + "supplier_payments"."refunded" <= "supplier_payments"."amount" AND ("supplier_payments"."status" = 'posted' OR "supplier_payments"."refunded" = 0));
```

- **Every change to the existing tables is quick.** The six new columns have a constant default, so Postgres does not
  rewrite the tables. The changed checks pass on every existing row (all the new columns are 0), and the rebuilt
  partial indexes are small.
- `meta/_journal.json` and `meta/0041_snapshot.json` change too. They are generated; commit them as they are.

### Migration 0042 (custom): RLS, what may change when, the sums

Run `pnpm --filter @omnivo/db generate --custom --name purchase-returns-debit-notes-rules`, then fill the file:

```sql
-- Custom SQL migration file, put your code below! --
-- 1) The seven new tenant tables: ENABLE + FORCE RLS + tenant_isolation (with NULLIF, as in 0002)
DO $$
DECLARE
  t text;
BEGIN
  FOR t IN
    SELECT unnest(ARRAY[
      'purchase_returns', 'purchase_return_lines', 'debit_notes', 'debit_note_lines',
      'debit_note_expenses', 'debit_note_allocations', 'supplier_refunds'
    ])
  LOOP
    EXECUTE format('ALTER TABLE %I ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY', t);
    EXECUTE format('ALTER TABLE %I FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY', t);
    EXECUTE format(
      'CREATE POLICY tenant_isolation ON %I
         USING (tenant_id = NULLIF(current_setting(''app.tenant_id'', true), '''')::uuid)
         WITH CHECK (tenant_id = NULLIF(current_setting(''app.tenant_id'', true), '''')::uuid)',
      t
    );
  END LOOP;
END $$;

-- 2) A purchase return is 0032's sales return the other way round: a draft is changed and deleted
--    freely, a posted one never changes, because what left the warehouse left.
--    Posting finishes what the API did first (17d.3 writes the lines, the receipt lines and the
--    order lines, then sets the return to posted last), under every path that writes:
--    - every line has its value;
--    - a line from a receipt line took that line's own lot, and only serial numbers that came in on
--      it (decision 15);
--    - it remembers the bill line that billed the receipt line, exactly when one had: a posted bill
--      line of that receipt line, or none and the receipt line not billed. A bill posted at the
--      same moment fails here or in its own check (section 8), never both pass;
--    - the receipt line counts it: its returned quantity is what the posted returns sent back, this
--      one included.
CREATE FUNCTION purchase_returns_guard() RETURNS trigger
LANGUAGE plpgsql AS $$
BEGIN
  IF OLD.status = 'posted' THEN
    RAISE EXCEPTION 'purchase return % is posted and cannot be changed or deleted', OLD.id
      USING ERRCODE = 'check_violation', CONSTRAINT = 'purchase_returns_posted_immutable';
  END IF;
  IF TG_OP = 'DELETE' THEN
    RETURN OLD;
  END IF;

  IF NEW.status = 'posted' THEN
    IF EXISTS (
         SELECT 1 FROM purchase_return_lines
          WHERE tenant_id = NEW.tenant_id AND return_id = NEW.id AND value IS NULL) THEN
      RAISE EXCEPTION 'purchase return % has lines with no value', OLD.id
        USING ERRCODE = 'check_violation', CONSTRAINT = 'purchase_returns_value_check';
    END IF;
    IF EXISTS (
         SELECT 1
           FROM purchase_return_lines l
           JOIN goods_receipt_lines gl ON gl.tenant_id = l.tenant_id AND gl.id = l.receipt_line_id
          WHERE l.tenant_id = NEW.tenant_id AND l.return_id = NEW.id
            AND (l.batch_id IS DISTINCT FROM gl.batch_id
                 OR NOT l.serial_numbers <@ gl.serial_numbers
                 OR (l.bill_line_id IS NULL AND gl.billed)
                 OR (l.bill_line_id IS NOT NULL AND NOT EXISTS (
                   SELECT 1
                     FROM bill_lines bl
                     JOIN bills b ON b.tenant_id = bl.tenant_id AND b.id = bl.bill_id
                    WHERE bl.tenant_id = l.tenant_id AND bl.id = l.bill_line_id
                      AND bl.receipt_line_id = l.receipt_line_id AND b.status = 'posted'))
                 OR gl.returned_quantity <> (
                   SELECT sum(o.base_quantity)
                     FROM purchase_return_lines o
                     JOIN purchase_returns r ON r.tenant_id = o.tenant_id AND r.id = o.return_id
                    WHERE o.tenant_id = l.tenant_id AND o.receipt_line_id = l.receipt_line_id
                      AND (r.status = 'posted' OR r.id = NEW.id)))) THEN
      RAISE EXCEPTION 'purchase return % does not match the goods receipt lines it sends back', OLD.id
        USING ERRCODE = 'check_violation', CONSTRAINT = 'purchase_returns_receipts_check';
    END IF;
  END IF;
  RETURN NEW;
END $$;

CREATE TRIGGER purchase_returns_guard
  BEFORE UPDATE OR DELETE ON purchase_returns
  FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION purchase_returns_guard();

-- The lines: only while the return is a draft, like a sales return's. One change is allowed on a
-- posted return's line: a debit note's posting adds to debited_quantity, with nothing else. It
-- only grows: a debit note is never undone. A line from a receipt line names a line of a posted
-- goods receipt of the return's supplier. When a draft is deleted its lines cascade; the header is
-- gone by then, so the lookup finds nothing and lets them go.
CREATE FUNCTION purchase_return_lines_guard() RETURNS trigger
LANGUAGE plpgsql AS $$
DECLARE
  v_supplier uuid;
BEGIN
  IF TG_OP = 'UPDATE' AND NEW.debited_quantity > OLD.debited_quantity
     AND to_jsonb(NEW) - 'debited_quantity' = to_jsonb(OLD) - 'debited_quantity' THEN
    RETURN NEW;
  END IF;
  IF (TG_OP <> 'INSERT' AND EXISTS (
        SELECT 1 FROM purchase_returns
         WHERE tenant_id = OLD.tenant_id AND id = OLD.return_id AND status = 'posted'))
     OR (TG_OP <> 'DELETE' AND EXISTS (
        SELECT 1 FROM purchase_returns
         WHERE tenant_id = NEW.tenant_id AND id = NEW.return_id AND status = 'posted')) THEN
    RAISE EXCEPTION 'the lines of a posted purchase return cannot be changed'
      USING ERRCODE = 'check_violation', CONSTRAINT = 'purchase_return_lines_posted_immutable';
  END IF;
  IF TG_OP = 'DELETE' THEN
    RETURN OLD;
  END IF;

  IF NEW.receipt_line_id IS NOT NULL THEN
    SELECT supplier_id INTO v_supplier
      FROM purchase_returns WHERE tenant_id = NEW.tenant_id AND id = NEW.return_id;
    -- NULL: no such return — the foreign key gives that error. The receipt line's own existence
    -- is its key's.
    IF v_supplier IS NOT NULL AND EXISTS (
         SELECT 1
           FROM goods_receipt_lines gl
           JOIN goods_receipts g ON g.tenant_id = gl.tenant_id AND g.id = gl.receipt_id
          WHERE gl.tenant_id = NEW.tenant_id AND gl.id = NEW.receipt_line_id
            AND (g.status <> 'posted' OR g.supplier_id <> v_supplier)) THEN
      RAISE EXCEPTION 'a purchase return line sends back a line of a posted goods receipt of its supplier'
        USING ERRCODE = 'check_violation', CONSTRAINT = 'purchase_return_lines_receipt_check';
    END IF;
  END IF;
  RETURN NEW;
END $$;

CREATE TRIGGER purchase_return_lines_guard
  BEFORE INSERT OR UPDATE OR DELETE ON purchase_return_lines
  FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION purchase_return_lines_guard();

-- 3) A debit note, 0032's credit note with a bill that may be missing:
--    - a draft is changed and deleted freely. With a bill, it debits a posted bill, is not dated
--      before it, and carries the bill's own branch and "prices include VAT" (decision 19): a line
--      debited in full then takes off exactly what it charged;
--    - posting needs something to take off: a line or an expense;
--    - a posted one is in the books and in the supplier's file: never deleted, never voided. Only
--      its money moves: applied (section 5's trigger; the API bumps the version) and refunded
--      (section 6's).
CREATE FUNCTION debit_notes_guard() RETURNS trigger
LANGUAGE plpgsql AS $$
DECLARE
  v_bill record;
BEGIN
  IF TG_OP <> 'INSERT' AND OLD.status = 'posted' THEN
    IF TG_OP = 'UPDATE'
       AND to_jsonb(NEW) - ARRAY['applied', 'refunded', 'version', 'updated_at', 'updated_by']
           = to_jsonb(OLD) - ARRAY['applied', 'refunded', 'version', 'updated_at', 'updated_by'] THEN
      RETURN NEW;
    END IF;
    RAISE EXCEPTION 'debit note % is posted and cannot be changed or deleted', OLD.id
      USING ERRCODE = 'check_violation', CONSTRAINT = 'debit_notes_posted_immutable';
  END IF;
  IF TG_OP = 'DELETE' THEN
    RETURN OLD;
  END IF;

  IF NEW.bill_id IS NOT NULL THEN
    SELECT status, date, branch_id, prices_include_vat INTO v_bill
      FROM bills WHERE tenant_id = NEW.tenant_id AND id = NEW.bill_id;
    -- Not found: no such bill — the foreign key gives that error
    IF FOUND AND (v_bill.status <> 'posted' OR NEW.date < v_bill.date
                  OR NEW.branch_id <> v_bill.branch_id
                  OR NEW.prices_include_vat <> v_bill.prices_include_vat) THEN
      RAISE EXCEPTION 'a debit note debits a posted bill, from its date, with its branch and prices'
        USING ERRCODE = 'check_violation', CONSTRAINT = 'debit_notes_bill_check';
    END IF;
  END IF;

  IF NEW.status = 'posted'
     AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM debit_note_lines
                      WHERE tenant_id = NEW.tenant_id AND debit_note_id = NEW.id)
     AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM debit_note_expenses
                      WHERE tenant_id = NEW.tenant_id AND debit_note_id = NEW.id) THEN
    RAISE EXCEPTION 'debit note % takes nothing off', NEW.id
      USING ERRCODE = 'check_violation', CONSTRAINT = 'debit_notes_lines_check';
  END IF;
  RETURN NEW;
END $$;

CREATE TRIGGER debit_notes_guard
  BEFORE INSERT OR UPDATE OR DELETE ON debit_notes
  FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION debit_notes_guard();

-- The lines: only while the debit note is a draft, like a credit note's. And what the keys cannot
-- see:
--    - a line with no bill belongs to a debit note with no bill (the key that holds bill_id is not
--      checked when it is NULL);
--    - a return line is of a posted return of the debit note's supplier: a draft return can still
--      change. Without a bill, it is a line on its own (decision 9): a receipt line's goods were
--      either billed (debit them on that bill) or not (the bill bills less).
CREATE FUNCTION debit_note_lines_guard() RETURNS trigger
LANGUAGE plpgsql AS $$
DECLARE
  v_note record;
BEGIN
  IF (TG_OP <> 'INSERT' AND EXISTS (
        SELECT 1 FROM debit_notes
         WHERE tenant_id = OLD.tenant_id AND id = OLD.debit_note_id AND status = 'posted'))
     OR (TG_OP <> 'DELETE' AND EXISTS (
        SELECT 1 FROM debit_notes
         WHERE tenant_id = NEW.tenant_id AND id = NEW.debit_note_id AND status = 'posted')) THEN
    RAISE EXCEPTION 'the lines of a posted debit note cannot be changed'
      USING ERRCODE = 'check_violation', CONSTRAINT = 'debit_note_lines_posted_immutable';
  END IF;
  IF TG_OP = 'DELETE' THEN
    RETURN OLD;
  END IF;

  SELECT supplier_id, bill_id INTO v_note
    FROM debit_notes WHERE tenant_id = NEW.tenant_id AND id = NEW.debit_note_id;
  -- Not found: no such debit note — the foreign key gives that error
  IF NOT FOUND THEN
    RETURN NEW;
  END IF;
  IF NEW.bill_id IS NULL AND v_note.bill_id IS NOT NULL THEN
    RAISE EXCEPTION 'a debit note line debits a line of its debit note''s bill'
      USING ERRCODE = 'check_violation', CONSTRAINT = 'debit_note_lines_bill_check';
  END IF;
  IF NEW.return_line_id IS NOT NULL AND EXISTS (
       SELECT 1
         FROM purchase_return_lines rl
         JOIN purchase_returns r ON r.tenant_id = rl.tenant_id AND r.id = rl.return_id
        WHERE rl.tenant_id = NEW.tenant_id AND rl.id = NEW.return_line_id
          AND (r.status <> 'posted' OR r.supplier_id <> v_note.supplier_id
               OR (NEW.bill_id IS NULL AND rl.receipt_line_id IS NOT NULL))) THEN
    RAISE EXCEPTION 'a debit note line takes money off a line of a posted return of its supplier'
      USING ERRCODE = 'check_violation', CONSTRAINT = 'debit_note_lines_return_check';
  END IF;
  RETURN NEW;
END $$;

CREATE TRIGGER debit_note_lines_guard
  BEFORE INSERT OR UPDATE OR DELETE ON debit_note_lines
  FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION debit_note_lines_guard();

-- The expenses: only while the debit note is a draft, checked before (OLD) and after (NEW)
CREATE FUNCTION debit_note_expenses_guard() RETURNS trigger
LANGUAGE plpgsql AS $$
BEGIN
  IF (TG_OP <> 'INSERT' AND EXISTS (
        SELECT 1 FROM debit_notes
         WHERE tenant_id = OLD.tenant_id AND id = OLD.debit_note_id AND status = 'posted'))
     OR (TG_OP <> 'DELETE' AND EXISTS (
        SELECT 1 FROM debit_notes
         WHERE tenant_id = NEW.tenant_id AND id = NEW.debit_note_id AND status = 'posted')) THEN
    RAISE EXCEPTION 'the expenses of a posted debit note cannot be changed'
      USING ERRCODE = 'check_violation', CONSTRAINT = 'debit_note_expenses_posted_immutable';
  END IF;
  IF TG_OP = 'DELETE' THEN
    RETURN OLD;
  END IF;
  RETURN NEW;
END $$;

CREATE TRIGGER debit_note_expenses_guard
  BEFORE INSERT OR UPDATE OR DELETE ON debit_note_expenses
  FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION debit_note_expenses_guard();

-- 4) A supplier refund is never deleted: like a payment, its number is on paper. While posted it
--    may be voided (status, the void date and reason), nothing else. A voided refund never changes
--    again. 0032's refund guard.
CREATE FUNCTION supplier_refunds_guard() RETURNS trigger
LANGUAGE plpgsql AS $$
BEGIN
  IF TG_OP = 'UPDATE' AND OLD.status = 'posted' AND NEW.status = 'voided'
     AND to_jsonb(NEW) - ARRAY['status', 'void_date', 'void_reason', 'version', 'updated_at',
                               'updated_by']
         = to_jsonb(OLD) - ARRAY['status', 'void_date', 'void_reason', 'version', 'updated_at',
                                 'updated_by'] THEN
    RETURN NEW;
  END IF;
  RAISE EXCEPTION 'supplier refund % can only be voided', OLD.id
    USING ERRCODE = 'check_violation', CONSTRAINT = 'supplier_refunds_immutable';
END $$;

CREATE TRIGGER supplier_refunds_guard
  BEFORE UPDATE OR DELETE ON supplier_refunds
  FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION supplier_refunds_guard();

-- 5) bills.amount_debited and debit_notes.applied are the sums of the debit note allocations:
--    0032's credit_note_allocations_apply with the bill's names. The table checks refuse what must
--    not happen: settling a bill past its total by payments and debit notes together, or a bill
--    that is not posted (bills_paid_check); applying more than the debit note has left, or
--    anything of a draft (debit_notes_money_check). The UPDATE locks the bill row, so a payment
--    and a debit note settling its last ৳5,000 at the same moment run one after the other, and
--    the second one fails on the check.
CREATE FUNCTION debit_note_allocations_apply() RETURNS trigger
LANGUAGE plpgsql AS $$
BEGIN
  IF TG_OP <> 'INSERT' THEN
    UPDATE bills SET amount_debited = amount_debited - OLD.amount
     WHERE tenant_id = OLD.tenant_id AND id = OLD.bill_id;
    UPDATE debit_notes SET applied = applied - OLD.amount
     WHERE tenant_id = OLD.tenant_id AND id = OLD.debit_note_id;
  END IF;
  IF TG_OP <> 'DELETE' THEN
    UPDATE bills SET amount_debited = amount_debited + NEW.amount
     WHERE tenant_id = NEW.tenant_id AND id = NEW.bill_id;
    UPDATE debit_notes SET applied = applied + NEW.amount
     WHERE tenant_id = NEW.tenant_id AND id = NEW.debit_note_id;
  END IF;
  RETURN NULL;
END $$;

CREATE TRIGGER debit_note_allocations_apply
  AFTER INSERT OR UPDATE OR DELETE ON debit_note_allocations
  FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION debit_note_allocations_apply();

-- 6) supplier_payments.refunded and debit_notes.refunded are the sums of the POSTED supplier
--    refunds that took money back out of them: 0032's refunds_apply with the purchase names. Only
--    one of the two UPDATEs finds a row (a refund has one source). The checks refuse taking back
--    more than the source has left (supplier_payments_amount_check, debit_notes_money_check), from
--    a draft debit note or a payment that is not posted (the same two checks).
CREATE FUNCTION supplier_refunds_apply() RETURNS trigger
LANGUAGE plpgsql AS $$
BEGIN
  IF TG_OP = 'UPDATE' AND OLD.status = 'posted' THEN
    UPDATE supplier_payments SET refunded = refunded - OLD.amount
     WHERE tenant_id = OLD.tenant_id AND id = OLD.payment_id;
    UPDATE debit_notes SET refunded = refunded - OLD.amount
     WHERE tenant_id = OLD.tenant_id AND id = OLD.debit_note_id;
  END IF;
  IF NEW.status = 'posted' THEN
    UPDATE supplier_payments SET refunded = refunded + NEW.amount
     WHERE tenant_id = NEW.tenant_id AND id = NEW.payment_id;
    UPDATE debit_notes SET refunded = refunded + NEW.amount
     WHERE tenant_id = NEW.tenant_id AND id = NEW.debit_note_id;
  END IF;
  RETURN NULL;
END $$;

CREATE TRIGGER supplier_refunds_apply
  AFTER INSERT OR UPDATE ON supplier_refunds
  FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION supplier_refunds_apply();

-- 7) 0040's supplier payment guard, with refunds. A posted payment may now also have its advance
--    taken back (refunded moves, by section 6's trigger). Voiding does not list refunded, and
--    supplier_payments_amount_check wants it at zero on anything but a posted payment, so a
--    payment with a posted refund cannot be voided (payment_has_refunds) until the refund is
--    voided first. The rest is unchanged.
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION supplier_payments_guard() RETURNS trigger
LANGUAGE plpgsql AS $$
DECLARE
  v_round text;
BEGIN
  IF TG_OP = 'DELETE' THEN
    IF OLD.status <> 'draft' OR OLD.number IS NOT NULL OR EXISTS (
         SELECT 1 FROM approval_rounds
          WHERE tenant_id = OLD.tenant_id AND document = 'supplier_payment'
            AND document_id = OLD.id) THEN
      RAISE EXCEPTION 'supplier payment % was submitted and cannot be deleted; cancel it instead', OLD.id
        USING ERRCODE = 'check_violation', CONSTRAINT = 'supplier_payments_submitted_immutable';
    END IF;
    RETURN OLD;
  END IF;

  IF NEW.supplier_bank_account_id IS NULL AND OLD.supplier_bank_account_id IS NOT NULL
     AND to_jsonb(NEW) - 'supplier_bank_account_id' = to_jsonb(OLD) - 'supplier_bank_account_id' THEN
    RETURN NEW;
  END IF;

  IF OLD.status = 'posted' AND (
       (NEW.status = 'posted'
        AND to_jsonb(NEW) - ARRAY['applied', 'refunded', 'version', 'updated_at', 'updated_by']
            = to_jsonb(OLD) - ARRAY['applied', 'refunded', 'version', 'updated_at', 'updated_by'])
       OR (NEW.status = 'voided'
        AND to_jsonb(NEW) - ARRAY['status', 'applied', 'void_date', 'void_reason', 'version',
                                  'updated_at', 'updated_by']
            = to_jsonb(OLD) - ARRAY['status', 'applied', 'void_date', 'void_reason', 'version',
                                    'updated_at', 'updated_by'])) THEN
    RETURN NEW;
  END IF;
  IF OLD.status IN ('posted', 'voided', 'cancelled') THEN
    RAISE EXCEPTION 'supplier payment % is %: it can only have its money applied or be voided', OLD.id, OLD.status
      USING ERRCODE = 'check_violation', CONSTRAINT = 'supplier_payments_posted_immutable';
  END IF;

  IF (OLD.number IS NOT NULL AND NEW.number IS DISTINCT FROM OLD.number)
     OR (OLD.status = 'pending'
         AND to_jsonb(NEW) - ARRAY['status', 'posted_at', 'posted_by', 'version', 'updated_at',
                                   'updated_by']
             <> to_jsonb(OLD) - ARRAY['status', 'posted_at', 'posted_by', 'version', 'updated_at',
                                      'updated_by']) THEN
    RAISE EXCEPTION 'supplier payment % is % and cannot be changed; reopen it first', OLD.id, OLD.status
      USING ERRCODE = 'check_violation', CONSTRAINT = 'supplier_payments_locked';
  END IF;
  IF NEW.status = OLD.status THEN
    RETURN NEW;
  END IF;

  IF (OLD.status, NEW.status) NOT IN (
       ('draft', 'pending'), ('draft', 'cancelled'), ('pending', 'posted'), ('pending', 'draft')) THEN
    RAISE EXCEPTION 'supplier payment % cannot go from % to %', OLD.id, OLD.status, NEW.status
      USING ERRCODE = 'check_violation', CONSTRAINT = 'supplier_payments_status_check';
  END IF;

  SELECT status INTO v_round
    FROM approval_rounds
   WHERE tenant_id = NEW.tenant_id AND document = 'supplier_payment' AND document_id = NEW.id
   ORDER BY submitted_at DESC, id DESC
   LIMIT 1;
  IF (NEW.status = 'pending' AND v_round IS DISTINCT FROM 'pending')
     OR (NEW.status = 'posted' AND v_round IS DISTINCT FROM 'approved')
     OR (OLD.status = 'pending' AND NEW.status = 'draft'
         AND coalesce(v_round, 'missing') NOT IN ('rejected', 'reopened')) THEN
    RAISE EXCEPTION 'supplier payment % cannot be % while its approval round is %',
        OLD.id, NEW.status, coalesce(v_round, 'missing')
      USING ERRCODE = 'check_violation', CONSTRAINT = 'supplier_payments_approval_check';
  END IF;
  RETURN NEW;
END $$;

-- 8) 0040's bill guards, with what debit notes and returns change:
--    - a posted bill may also have debit notes' money applied (amount_debited, section 5's
--      trigger) and its debited total grow (debit_note_total, written by a debit note's posting
--      through Drizzle, which also sets updated_at and may set updated_by). Never down: a debit
--      note is never undone. version still never moves, so a bill page open in another tab stays
--      current;
--    - posting also checks that each receipt line is billed for what was kept: a return posted
--      after the draft was written left the bill line too big (decision 17). The rest is
--      unchanged.
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION bills_guard() RETURNS trigger
LANGUAGE plpgsql AS $$
DECLARE
  v_round text;
BEGIN
  IF TG_OP = 'DELETE' THEN
    IF OLD.status <> 'draft' OR OLD.number IS NOT NULL OR EXISTS (
         SELECT 1 FROM approval_rounds
          WHERE tenant_id = OLD.tenant_id AND document = 'bill' AND document_id = OLD.id) THEN
      RAISE EXCEPTION 'bill % was submitted and cannot be deleted; cancel it instead', OLD.id
        USING ERRCODE = 'check_violation', CONSTRAINT = 'bills_submitted_immutable';
    END IF;
    RETURN OLD;
  END IF;

  IF OLD.status IN ('posted', 'cancelled') THEN
    IF OLD.status = 'posted' AND NEW.debit_note_total >= OLD.debit_note_total
       AND to_jsonb(NEW) - ARRAY['amount_paid', 'amount_debited', 'debit_note_total', 'updated_at',
                                 'updated_by']
           = to_jsonb(OLD) - ARRAY['amount_paid', 'amount_debited', 'debit_note_total',
                                   'updated_at', 'updated_by'] THEN
      RETURN NEW;
    END IF;
    RAISE EXCEPTION 'bill % is % and cannot be changed', OLD.id, OLD.status
      USING ERRCODE = 'check_violation', CONSTRAINT = 'bills_posted_immutable';
  END IF;

  IF (OLD.number IS NOT NULL AND NEW.number IS DISTINCT FROM OLD.number)
     OR (OLD.status = 'pending'
         AND to_jsonb(NEW) - ARRAY['status', 'posted_at', 'posted_by', 'version', 'updated_at',
                                   'updated_by']
             <> to_jsonb(OLD) - ARRAY['status', 'posted_at', 'posted_by', 'version', 'updated_at',
                                      'updated_by']) THEN
    RAISE EXCEPTION 'bill % is % and cannot be changed; reopen it first', OLD.id, OLD.status
      USING ERRCODE = 'check_violation', CONSTRAINT = 'bills_locked';
  END IF;
  IF NEW.status = OLD.status THEN
    RETURN NEW;
  END IF;

  IF (OLD.status, NEW.status) NOT IN (
       ('draft', 'pending'), ('draft', 'cancelled'), ('pending', 'posted'), ('pending', 'draft')) THEN
    RAISE EXCEPTION 'bill % cannot go from % to %', OLD.id, OLD.status, NEW.status
      USING ERRCODE = 'check_violation', CONSTRAINT = 'bills_status_check';
  END IF;

  SELECT status INTO v_round
    FROM approval_rounds
   WHERE tenant_id = NEW.tenant_id AND document = 'bill' AND document_id = NEW.id
   ORDER BY submitted_at DESC, id DESC
   LIMIT 1;
  IF (NEW.status = 'pending' AND v_round IS DISTINCT FROM 'pending')
     OR (NEW.status = 'posted' AND v_round IS DISTINCT FROM 'approved')
     OR (OLD.status = 'pending' AND NEW.status = 'draft'
         AND coalesce(v_round, 'missing') NOT IN ('rejected', 'reopened')) THEN
    RAISE EXCEPTION 'bill % cannot be % while its approval round is %',
        OLD.id, NEW.status, coalesce(v_round, 'missing')
      USING ERRCODE = 'check_violation', CONSTRAINT = 'bills_approval_check';
  END IF;

  IF NEW.status = 'posted' THEN
    IF EXISTS (
         SELECT 1
           FROM bill_lines bl
           LEFT JOIN goods_receipt_lines gl
             ON gl.tenant_id = bl.tenant_id AND gl.id = bl.receipt_line_id
           JOIN products p ON p.tenant_id = bl.tenant_id AND p.id = bl.product_id
          WHERE bl.tenant_id = NEW.tenant_id AND bl.bill_id = NEW.id
            AND (gl.billed IS FALSE
                 OR bl.base_quantity <> gl.base_quantity - gl.returned_quantity
                 OR (bl.receipt_line_id IS NULL AND bl.order_line_id IS NULL
                     AND p.type = 'goods')
                 OR EXISTS (
                   SELECT 1
                     FROM bill_lines other
                     JOIN bills b ON b.tenant_id = other.tenant_id AND b.id = other.bill_id
                    WHERE other.tenant_id = bl.tenant_id
                      AND other.receipt_line_id = bl.receipt_line_id
                      AND other.bill_id <> bl.bill_id AND b.status = 'posted'))) THEN
      RAISE EXCEPTION 'bill % has goods lines that are not received, or billed by another bill', OLD.id
        USING ERRCODE = 'check_violation', CONSTRAINT = 'bills_receipts_check';
    END IF;
    -- The service lines' order lines are locked first, in id order: a second bill posting the
    -- same line at the same moment waits here, and then sees this one posted
    PERFORM 1
       FROM purchase_order_lines pl
      WHERE pl.tenant_id = NEW.tenant_id
        AND pl.id IN (SELECT bl.order_line_id
                        FROM bill_lines bl
                       WHERE bl.tenant_id = NEW.tenant_id AND bl.bill_id = NEW.id
                         AND bl.receipt_line_id IS NULL AND bl.order_line_id IS NOT NULL)
      ORDER BY pl.id
        FOR NO KEY UPDATE;
    IF EXISTS (
         SELECT 1
           FROM bill_lines bl
           JOIN bill_lines other
             ON other.tenant_id = bl.tenant_id AND other.order_line_id = bl.order_line_id
            AND other.receipt_line_id IS NULL AND other.bill_id <> bl.bill_id
           JOIN bills b ON b.tenant_id = other.tenant_id AND b.id = other.bill_id
          WHERE bl.tenant_id = NEW.tenant_id AND bl.bill_id = NEW.id
            AND bl.receipt_line_id IS NULL AND bl.order_line_id IS NOT NULL
            AND b.status = 'posted') THEN
      RAISE EXCEPTION 'bill % bills an order line another posted bill billed', OLD.id
        USING ERRCODE = 'check_violation', CONSTRAINT = 'bills_order_lines_check';
    END IF;
  END IF;
  RETURN NEW;
END $$;

-- The lines: 0040's guard, with two changes. A posted bill's line may have what debit notes took
-- off grow (debited), with nothing else. And a receipt line is billed for what was kept (base −
-- returned, contracts' keptQuantity), no longer the whole line.
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION bill_lines_guard() RETURNS trigger
LANGUAGE plpgsql AS $$
DECLARE
  v_status text;
  v_supplier uuid;
  v_own boolean := false;
  v_receipt record;
  v_order record;
BEGIN
  IF TG_OP = 'UPDATE' AND NEW.debited > OLD.debited
     AND to_jsonb(NEW) - 'debited' = to_jsonb(OLD) - 'debited'
     AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM bills
                  WHERE tenant_id = OLD.tenant_id AND id = OLD.bill_id AND status = 'posted') THEN
    RETURN NEW;
  END IF;
  -- 0040's section 2 change. Only a service line's: a receipt line's order has a goods receipt, so
  -- it is never reopened, and its copy of the order line must stay.
  IF TG_OP = 'UPDATE' AND NEW.order_line_id IS NULL AND OLD.order_line_id IS NOT NULL
     AND OLD.receipt_line_id IS NULL
     AND to_jsonb(NEW) - 'order_line_id' = to_jsonb(OLD) - 'order_line_id' THEN
    RETURN NEW;
  END IF;

  IF TG_OP <> 'INSERT' THEN
    SELECT status INTO v_status FROM bills WHERE tenant_id = OLD.tenant_id AND id = OLD.bill_id;
    v_own := TG_OP = 'UPDATE' AND v_status = 'pending'
      AND OLD.receipt_line_id IS NULL AND OLD.order_line_id IS NULL
      AND NEW.receipt_line_id IS NOT NULL
      AND to_jsonb(NEW) - 'receipt_line_id' = to_jsonb(OLD) - 'receipt_line_id';
    -- NULL: a deleted draft's cascade
    IF v_status IS NOT NULL AND v_status <> 'draft' AND NOT v_own THEN
      RAISE EXCEPTION 'the lines of a % bill cannot be changed', v_status
        USING ERRCODE = 'check_violation', CONSTRAINT = 'bill_lines_locked';
    END IF;
    IF TG_OP = 'DELETE' THEN
      RETURN OLD;
    END IF;
  END IF;

  -- The bill the line is (or moves) in must be a draft too
  SELECT status, supplier_id INTO v_status, v_supplier
    FROM bills WHERE tenant_id = NEW.tenant_id AND id = NEW.bill_id;
  -- NULL: no such bill — the foreign key gives that error
  IF v_status IS NULL THEN
    RETURN NEW;
  END IF;
  IF v_status <> 'draft' AND NOT v_own THEN
    RAISE EXCEPTION 'lines cannot be added to a % bill', v_status
      USING ERRCODE = 'check_violation', CONSTRAINT = 'bill_lines_locked';
  END IF;

  IF NEW.receipt_line_id IS NOT NULL THEN
    SELECT r.supplier_id, r.status, r.bill_id, l.order_line_id, l.base_quantity,
           l.returned_quantity
      INTO v_receipt
      FROM goods_receipt_lines l
      JOIN goods_receipts r ON r.tenant_id = l.tenant_id AND r.id = l.receipt_id
     WHERE l.tenant_id = NEW.tenant_id AND l.id = NEW.receipt_line_id;
    -- Not found: the foreign key gives that error. A receipt a bill made is billed by that bill
    -- only, and only by its posting.
    IF FOUND AND (v_receipt.supplier_id <> v_supplier OR v_receipt.status <> 'posted'
                  OR v_receipt.base_quantity - v_receipt.returned_quantity <> NEW.base_quantity
                  OR v_receipt.order_line_id IS DISTINCT FROM NEW.order_line_id
                  OR v_receipt.bill_id IS DISTINCT FROM (CASE WHEN v_own THEN NEW.bill_id END)) THEN
      RAISE EXCEPTION 'a bill line bills what was kept of a line of a posted goods receipt of its supplier'
        USING ERRCODE = 'check_violation', CONSTRAINT = 'bill_lines_receipt_check';
    END IF;
  ELSIF NEW.order_line_id IS NOT NULL THEN
    SELECT o.supplier_id, o.status, p.type
      INTO v_order
      FROM purchase_order_lines l
      JOIN purchase_orders o ON o.tenant_id = l.tenant_id AND o.id = l.order_id
      JOIN products p ON p.tenant_id = l.tenant_id AND p.id = l.product_id
     WHERE l.tenant_id = NEW.tenant_id AND l.id = NEW.order_line_id;
    IF FOUND AND (v_order.supplier_id <> v_supplier
                  OR v_order.status NOT IN ('approved', 'received', 'closed')
                  OR v_order.type <> 'service') THEN
      RAISE EXCEPTION 'a bill line bills a service line of an approved purchase order of its supplier'
        USING ERRCODE = 'check_violation', CONSTRAINT = 'bill_lines_order_check';
    END IF;
  END IF;
  RETURN NEW;
END $$;

-- The expenses: 0040's guard, and a posted bill's expense may have debited grow, with nothing else
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION bill_expenses_guard() RETURNS trigger
LANGUAGE plpgsql AS $$
BEGIN
  IF TG_OP = 'UPDATE' AND NEW.debited > OLD.debited
     AND to_jsonb(NEW) - 'debited' = to_jsonb(OLD) - 'debited'
     AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM bills
                  WHERE tenant_id = OLD.tenant_id AND id = OLD.bill_id AND status = 'posted') THEN
    RETURN NEW;
  END IF;
  IF (TG_OP <> 'INSERT' AND EXISTS (
        SELECT 1 FROM bills
         WHERE tenant_id = OLD.tenant_id AND id = OLD.bill_id AND status <> 'draft'))
     OR (TG_OP <> 'DELETE' AND EXISTS (
        SELECT 1 FROM bills
         WHERE tenant_id = NEW.tenant_id AND id = NEW.bill_id AND status <> 'draft')) THEN
    RAISE EXCEPTION 'the expenses of a bill change only while it is a draft'
      USING ERRCODE = 'check_violation', CONSTRAINT = 'bill_expenses_locked';
  END IF;
  IF TG_OP = 'DELETE' THEN
    RETURN OLD;
  END IF;
  RETURN NEW;
END $$;

-- 9) 0040's goods receipt line guard, with returns. Two changes are allowed on a posted receipt's
--    line, each on its own: it becomes billed (false → true, once), or a return's posting adds to
--    returned_quantity (only up: a posted return is never undone). Like 0032's challan line.
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION goods_receipt_lines_guard() RETURNS trigger
LANGUAGE plpgsql AS $$
DECLARE
  v_status text;
  v_order uuid;
BEGIN
  IF TG_OP <> 'INSERT' THEN
    SELECT status INTO v_status
      FROM goods_receipts WHERE tenant_id = OLD.tenant_id AND id = OLD.receipt_id;
    IF v_status = 'posted' THEN
      IF TG_OP = 'UPDATE' AND NOT OLD.billed AND NEW.billed
         AND to_jsonb(NEW) - 'billed' = to_jsonb(OLD) - 'billed' THEN
        RETURN NEW;
      END IF;
      IF TG_OP = 'UPDATE' AND NEW.returned_quantity > OLD.returned_quantity
         AND to_jsonb(NEW) - 'returned_quantity' = to_jsonb(OLD) - 'returned_quantity' THEN
        RETURN NEW;
      END IF;
      RAISE EXCEPTION 'the lines of a posted goods receipt cannot be changed'
        USING ERRCODE = 'check_violation', CONSTRAINT = 'goods_receipt_lines_posted_immutable';
    END IF;
    -- NULL: a deleted draft's cascade
    IF TG_OP = 'DELETE' THEN
      RETURN OLD;
    END IF;
  END IF;

  SELECT status, order_id INTO v_status, v_order
    FROM goods_receipts WHERE tenant_id = NEW.tenant_id AND id = NEW.receipt_id;
  -- Not found: no such receipt — the foreign key gives that error
  IF NOT FOUND THEN
    RETURN NEW;
  END IF;
  IF v_status = 'posted' THEN
    RAISE EXCEPTION 'the lines of a posted goods receipt cannot be changed'
      USING ERRCODE = 'check_violation', CONSTRAINT = 'goods_receipt_lines_posted_immutable';
  END IF;
  IF NEW.billed THEN
    RAISE EXCEPTION 'only a line of a posted goods receipt is billed'
      USING ERRCODE = 'check_violation', CONSTRAINT = 'goods_receipt_lines_billed_check';
  END IF;
  -- Nothing goes back from goods that are not in stock yet
  IF NEW.returned_quantity <> 0 THEN
    RAISE EXCEPTION 'only a line of a posted goods receipt is sent back'
      USING ERRCODE = 'check_violation', CONSTRAINT = 'goods_receipt_lines_returned_check';
  END IF;
  -- Another order than the receipt's is the line's key's error (goods_receipt_lines_receipt_fk);
  -- this is the case the key cannot see
  IF NEW.order_id IS NULL AND v_order IS NOT NULL THEN
    RAISE EXCEPTION 'a goods receipt line copies its receipt''s purchase order'
      USING ERRCODE = 'check_violation', CONSTRAINT = 'goods_receipt_lines_order_check';
  END IF;
  RETURN NEW;
END $$;

-- 10) A return before billing gives the order its goods back (decision 3): the order line's
--     received quantity goes down, and a received order is approved again ("Partly received"), so
--     the supplier can send the goods again on the same order. 0040's order guard, with that one
--     new move: received → approved, only the status changing, and only while a goods line is
--     short. It keeps its approval: its newest round is still approved.
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION purchase_orders_guard() RETURNS trigger
LANGUAGE plpgsql AS $$
DECLARE
  v_round text;
BEGIN
  IF TG_OP = 'DELETE' THEN
    IF OLD.status <> 'draft' OR OLD.number IS NOT NULL OR EXISTS (
         SELECT 1 FROM approval_rounds
          WHERE tenant_id = OLD.tenant_id AND document = 'purchase_order'
            AND document_id = OLD.id) THEN
      RAISE EXCEPTION 'purchase order % was submitted and cannot be deleted; cancel it instead', OLD.id
        USING ERRCODE = 'check_violation', CONSTRAINT = 'purchase_orders_submitted_immutable';
    END IF;
    RETURN OLD;
  END IF;

  IF (OLD.number IS NOT NULL AND NEW.number IS DISTINCT FROM OLD.number)
     OR (OLD.status <> 'draft'
         AND to_jsonb(NEW) - ARRAY['status', 'version', 'updated_at', 'updated_by']
             <> to_jsonb(OLD) - ARRAY['status', 'version', 'updated_at', 'updated_by']) THEN
    RAISE EXCEPTION 'purchase order % is % and cannot be changed; reopen it first', OLD.id, OLD.status
      USING ERRCODE = 'check_violation', CONSTRAINT = 'purchase_orders_locked';
  END IF;
  -- A draft that moves to another warehouse keeps no line of a requisition for the old one
  -- (decision 16; section 7 checks each line as it is written)
  IF NEW.warehouse_id <> OLD.warehouse_id AND EXISTS (
       SELECT 1
         FROM purchase_order_lines pl
         JOIN requisition_lines rl ON rl.tenant_id = pl.tenant_id AND rl.id = pl.requisition_line_id
         JOIN requisitions r ON r.tenant_id = rl.tenant_id AND r.id = rl.requisition_id
        WHERE pl.tenant_id = NEW.tenant_id AND pl.order_id = NEW.id
          AND r.warehouse_id <> NEW.warehouse_id) THEN
    RAISE EXCEPTION 'purchase order % buys for a requisition of another warehouse', OLD.id
      USING ERRCODE = 'check_violation', CONSTRAINT = 'purchase_order_lines_requisition_check';
  END IF;
  IF NEW.status = OLD.status THEN
    RETURN NEW;
  END IF;

  IF (OLD.status, NEW.status) NOT IN (
       ('draft', 'pending'), ('draft', 'cancelled'),
       ('pending', 'approved'), ('pending', 'draft'),
       ('approved', 'draft'), ('approved', 'received'), ('approved', 'closed'),
       ('approved', 'cancelled'), ('received', 'approved')) THEN
    RAISE EXCEPTION 'purchase order % cannot go from % to %', OLD.id, OLD.status, NEW.status
      USING ERRCODE = 'check_violation', CONSTRAINT = 'purchase_orders_status_check';
  END IF;

  IF (OLD.status = 'approved' AND NEW.status IN ('draft', 'cancelled') AND EXISTS (
        SELECT 1 FROM goods_receipts WHERE tenant_id = NEW.tenant_id AND order_id = NEW.id))
     OR (NEW.status = 'closed' AND NOT EXISTS (
        SELECT 1 FROM goods_receipts
         WHERE tenant_id = NEW.tenant_id AND order_id = NEW.id AND status = 'posted')
        AND NOT EXISTS (
        SELECT 1
          FROM purchase_order_lines pl
          JOIN bill_lines bl ON bl.tenant_id = pl.tenant_id AND bl.order_line_id = pl.id
          JOIN bills b ON b.tenant_id = bl.tenant_id AND b.id = bl.bill_id
         WHERE pl.tenant_id = NEW.tenant_id AND pl.order_id = NEW.id AND b.status = 'posted'))
     OR (NEW.status = 'received' AND EXISTS (
        SELECT 1
          FROM purchase_order_lines pl
          JOIN products p ON p.tenant_id = pl.tenant_id AND p.id = pl.product_id
         WHERE pl.tenant_id = NEW.tenant_id AND pl.order_id = NEW.id
           AND p.type = 'goods' AND pl.received_quantity < pl.base_quantity))
     OR (OLD.status = 'received' AND NOT EXISTS (
        SELECT 1
          FROM purchase_order_lines pl
          JOIN products p ON p.tenant_id = pl.tenant_id AND p.id = pl.product_id
         WHERE pl.tenant_id = NEW.tenant_id AND pl.order_id = NEW.id
           AND p.type = 'goods' AND pl.received_quantity < pl.base_quantity)) THEN
    RAISE EXCEPTION 'purchase order % cannot be % with the goods receipts it has', OLD.id, NEW.status
      USING ERRCODE = 'check_violation', CONSTRAINT = 'purchase_orders_receipts_check';
  END IF;
  IF OLD.status = 'approved' AND NEW.status IN ('draft', 'cancelled') AND EXISTS (
       SELECT 1
         FROM purchase_order_lines pl
         JOIN bill_lines bl ON bl.tenant_id = pl.tenant_id AND bl.order_line_id = pl.id
         JOIN bills b ON b.tenant_id = bl.tenant_id AND b.id = bl.bill_id
        WHERE pl.tenant_id = NEW.tenant_id AND pl.order_id = NEW.id AND b.status <> 'cancelled') THEN
    RAISE EXCEPTION 'purchase order % is billed and cannot be %', OLD.id, NEW.status
      USING ERRCODE = 'check_violation', CONSTRAINT = 'purchase_orders_bills_check';
  END IF;

  SELECT status INTO v_round
    FROM approval_rounds
   WHERE tenant_id = NEW.tenant_id AND document = 'purchase_order' AND document_id = NEW.id
   ORDER BY submitted_at DESC, id DESC
   LIMIT 1;
  IF (NEW.status = 'pending' AND v_round IS DISTINCT FROM 'pending')
     OR (NEW.status = 'approved' AND v_round IS DISTINCT FROM 'approved')
     OR (OLD.status = 'pending' AND NEW.status = 'draft'
         AND coalesce(v_round, 'missing') NOT IN ('rejected', 'reopened')) THEN
    RAISE EXCEPTION 'purchase order % cannot be % while its approval round is %',
        OLD.id, NEW.status, coalesce(v_round, 'missing')
      USING ERRCODE = 'check_violation', CONSTRAINT = 'purchase_orders_approval_check';
  END IF;
  RETURN NEW;
END $$;

-- The lines: 0038's guard, and a return before billing may lower what was received, with nothing
-- else: on an approved order (partly received), a received one (the line goes down first, then the
-- order goes back to approved) and a closed one (it stays closed). Never what was turned back.
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION purchase_order_lines_guard() RETURNS trigger
LANGUAGE plpgsql AS $$
DECLARE
  v_status text;
  v_warehouse uuid;
  v_req_status text;
  v_req_warehouse uuid;
BEGIN
  IF TG_OP = 'UPDATE' AND NEW.requisition_line_id IS NULL AND OLD.requisition_line_id IS NOT NULL
     AND to_jsonb(NEW) - 'requisition_line_id' = to_jsonb(OLD) - 'requisition_line_id' THEN
    RETURN NEW;
  END IF;

  IF TG_OP <> 'INSERT' THEN
    SELECT status, warehouse_id INTO v_status, v_warehouse
      FROM purchase_orders WHERE tenant_id = OLD.tenant_id AND id = OLD.order_id;
    IF TG_OP = 'UPDATE' AND v_status = 'approved'
       AND NEW.received_quantity >= OLD.received_quantity
       AND NEW.rejected_quantity >= OLD.rejected_quantity
       AND to_jsonb(NEW) - ARRAY['received_quantity', 'rejected_quantity']
           = to_jsonb(OLD) - ARRAY['received_quantity', 'rejected_quantity'] THEN
      RETURN NEW;
    END IF;
    IF TG_OP = 'UPDATE' AND v_status IN ('approved', 'received', 'closed')
       AND NEW.received_quantity < OLD.received_quantity
       AND to_jsonb(NEW) - 'received_quantity' = to_jsonb(OLD) - 'received_quantity' THEN
      RETURN NEW;
    END IF;
    -- NULL: a deleted draft's cascade
    IF v_status IS NOT NULL AND v_status <> 'draft' THEN
      RAISE EXCEPTION 'the lines of a % purchase order cannot be changed, except what was received', v_status
        USING ERRCODE = 'check_violation', CONSTRAINT = 'purchase_order_lines_locked';
    END IF;
    IF TG_OP = 'DELETE' THEN
      RETURN OLD;
    END IF;
  END IF;

  -- The order the line is (or moves) in must be a draft too
  SELECT status, warehouse_id INTO v_status, v_warehouse
    FROM purchase_orders WHERE tenant_id = NEW.tenant_id AND id = NEW.order_id;
  -- NULL: no such order — the foreign key gives that error
  IF v_status IS NOT NULL AND v_status <> 'draft' THEN
    RAISE EXCEPTION 'lines cannot be added to a % purchase order', v_status
      USING ERRCODE = 'check_violation', CONSTRAINT = 'purchase_order_lines_locked';
  END IF;

  IF NEW.requisition_line_id IS NOT NULL THEN
    SELECT r.status, r.warehouse_id INTO v_req_status, v_req_warehouse
      FROM requisition_lines rl
      JOIN requisitions r ON r.tenant_id = rl.tenant_id AND r.id = rl.requisition_id
     WHERE rl.tenant_id = NEW.tenant_id AND rl.id = NEW.requisition_line_id
       FOR SHARE OF r;
    -- NULL: no such requisition line — the foreign key gives that error
    IF v_req_status IS NOT NULL
       AND (v_req_status NOT IN ('approved', 'closed') OR v_req_warehouse <> v_warehouse) THEN
      RAISE EXCEPTION 'an order line buys only for an approved requisition of the order''s warehouse'
        USING ERRCODE = 'check_violation', CONSTRAINT = 'purchase_order_lines_requisition_check';
    END IF;
  END IF;
  RETURN NEW;
END $$;
```

- **Section 1** is the same loop as every step, on the seven tables.
- **Section 2, the return.**
  - The header guard is 0032's: a posted return never changes and is never deleted.
  - **Posting checks four things the API did just before** (decision 28; 17d.3 writes the lines, the receipt lines and
    the order lines, then sets the return to posted last). Every line has a value. A line from a receipt line carries
    that line's own lot (`IS DISTINCT FROM`, so "no lot" on both sides is equal) and only serial numbers that came in
    on it (`<@` is "is contained in"). It names a posted bill line of that receipt line exactly when the receipt line
    is billed. And the receipt line's `returned_quantity` equals the posted returns' lines plus this one's: the
    API did add this return to it. Each check reads with a join, once per posting.
  - **The race it closes.** A bill posting marks the receipt line billed under the row's lock; a return posting adds
    to `returned_quantity` under the same lock. Whichever comes second waits, and then fails: the bill on
    `bills_receipts_check` (the line is no longer the kept quantity), or the return on this check (it said "not
    billed", and the line now is).
  - The line guard is 0032's, with `debited_quantity` in place of `credited_quantity`, plus one check the keys cannot
    make: the receipt line is of a POSTED goods receipt of the return's supplier.
- **Section 3, the debit note.**
  - Draft: free, but with a bill, the bill must be posted, not dated after the debit note (`debit_note_date`), with
    the same branch and "prices include VAT" (decision 30). A posting needs a line or an expense.
  - Posted: only `applied` and `refunded` move (and the version, which the API bumps when the money is applied again).
    No void, like a credit note ("Not in this step, on purpose").
  - The line guard is the credit note's, plus two checks. A line with no bill in a debit note that has one (the case
    the key cannot see). And a return line must be of a POSTED return of the same supplier: a draft return's line can
    still change or be deleted. Without a bill, it must be a line on its own (decision 9): a line from a receipt line
    was either billed (debit it on that bill) or not (the bill billed less).
  - The expenses change only while the debit note is a draft.
- **Section 4, the refund guard,** 0032's.
- **Section 5, `debit_note_allocations_apply`,** 0032's credit note trigger with the bill's names. No guard on the
  allocations: the two checks already refuse a draft debit note (`debit_notes_money_check`) and a bill that is not
  posted (`bills_paid_check`). The `UPDATE bills` locks the bill row, so a payment and a debit note settling its last
  money run one after the other.
- **Section 6, `supplier_refunds_apply`,** 0032's refund trigger. Only one of the two `UPDATE`s finds a row.
- **Section 7, the payment guard again.** One word changes: a posted payment may also move `refunded`. The whole
  function is written again because `CREATE OR REPLACE` needs the whole body. The void branch does not list
  `refunded`, so a payment with a refund cannot be voided (the amount check refuses it anyway).
- **Section 8, the bill guards again.**
  - A posted bill may also move `amount_debited` and `debit_note_total` (never down), plus `updated_at` and
    `updated_by`: the debit note's posting writes `debit_note_total` through Drizzle, which sets them. `version` still
    may not move (decision 31).
  - Posting adds one condition: `bl.base_quantity <> gl.base_quantity - gl.returned_quantity` (decision 29). For a
    line of the bill's own receipt `returned_quantity` is 0, and for a line with no receipt line `gl` is NULL, so the
    comparison is NULL and adds nothing.
  - The line guard's first `IF` lets a posted bill's line grow `debited` alone. It comes first, before the "not a
    draft" error. The receipt line check compares with the kept quantity, and its message says so.
  - The expense guard lets a posted bill's expense grow `debited` alone.
- **Section 9, the goods receipt line guard again:** a posted line may grow `returned_quantity` alone, like a challan
  line in 0032. A draft line has nothing returned: its goods are not in stock yet.
- **Section 10, the purchase order again** (decision 3).
  - The order guard has one new move, `received → approved`, with only the status changing (the `purchase_orders_locked`
    check above it already allows only that). It needs a goods line that is short: a received order with everything
    in is not "partly received". It keeps its approval: its newest round is still approved.
  - The line guard lets `received_quantity` go down alone on an approved, received or closed order. On a received
    order the API lowers the line first, then moves the order. A closed order stays closed (17d.1): the goods are no
    longer coming. `rejected_quantity` never goes down: what was turned back was turned back.

> **What we checked.** On a throwaway database with every migration up to 0042, as `omnivo_app` (115 checks, plus
> three races in two sessions). Goods receipt lines: a draft line could not send anything back; a posted line could not
> send back more than it accepted, nothing from a line that accepted nothing, and not together with another change. A
> return line could not come from another supplier's receipt or a draft receipt, be for another item than its receipt
> line, name a bill line without its bill, start debited, or be for 0. Posting a return failed without a value, with
> the wrong lot, with a serial number that did not come in, and before the receipt line counted it; then it posted, and
> its header, lines and the count could not change. The order line's received quantity went down on an approved
> order, but not with the rejected quantity; a received order could not go back to approved while full, went back once
> a return made a line short, and its line could not go up meanwhile; a closed order's line went down, never up. A bill
> line for the whole receipt line failed after a return; for what was kept it posted. A return of 5 m posted while a
> bill for 30 m waited made the bill's posting fail; reopened and written for 25 m, it posted. A return after the bill
> failed until it named the bill line (another bill's line failed), then posted; the billed line could not go back. A
> draft return was deleted with its lines. A debit note for a bill with another branch, other prices, an earlier date,
> a draft bill or another supplier's bill failed, as did a credit note date without its number and an empty number;
> posting with nothing on it failed. Its lines refused a return line the bill line had not billed, another item, a
> line of another bill, no bill line, and no bill in a debit note with one; its expenses refused the same expense twice,
> an unknown expense and ৳0. Posted, it refused changes, deletion, line and expense changes. A bill line's and an
> expense's `debited` grew, never past the total, never down, not with another change; a return line's
> `debited_quantity` grew to what went back; the bill's debited total grew, never past the total or down, and the
> bill's version could not move; a draft bill could have none. Allocations: a draft debit note's, one on a draft bill
> and one on another supplier's bill failed; applied, the bill and the debit note followed, more than the debit note
> failed, changed and removed, both followed; a payment for more than the bill still owed after the debit note could
> not post. A debit note without a bill took a return line on its own; a return line from a receipt, a draft return's
> line, another item, no return line and an expense failed; it posted, and its line on its own was debited. A draft
> debit note was deleted with its lines. Refunds: part of an advance came back; more than was left, then applying the
> rest of it, a draft payment, two sources, none, another supplier and ৳0 failed; the payment could not be voided while
> refunded. A debit note's money came back once, then neither a second refund nor an allocation fit; a draft debit
> note's failed. A refund refused changes and deletion, a void date before its date and a 201-character reason; voided,
> the advance was back, the refund froze, and the payment could then be voided. `purchase_return`,
> `purchase_debit_note` and `purchase_refund` entries needed their documents. Another workspace saw none of the seven
> tables, could not write into them, and changed and deleted nothing; with no workspace nothing was visible. The three
> permissions were in the catalog. Races: two returns sending back the last 15 m of a 20 m line (the second waited, then
> failed on `goods_receipt_lines_returned_check`); a bill posting a receipt line while a return of it, as not billed,
> was posted (the return waited, then failed on `purchase_returns_receipts_check`); a payment and a debit note settling
> the last money of one bill (the debit note waited, then failed on `bills_paid_check`). 17c's 150 database checks
> still pass on top of 0042. 17b's checks pass too, with two lines changed on purpose: an approved order's received
> quantity may now go down, and a full received order going back to approved now fails on
> `purchase_orders_receipts_check` instead of `purchase_orders_status_check`. On a second database migrated to 0040 and
> filled by 17c's checks, 0041 and 0042 applied, and every existing row came through with nothing returned, debited or
> refunded. `drizzle-kit generate` then reports no schema changes.

### Check this part

```bash
pnpm --filter @omnivo/contracts build
pnpm --filter @omnivo/db typecheck
pnpm lint
```

`packages/db` reads the contract from its build, so build it first after 17d.1. The whole repo still does not
type-check: 17d.1's gaps in the translations, the API and the app are still open (17d.3, 17d.5, 17d.6).

Then run `pnpm db:migrate` against your dev database. It applies 0041 and 0042 and adds the three permissions. Your
existing bills, receipts and payments are untouched: every new column starts at 0.

## 17d.3 — `apps/api`: returns, debit notes and refunds

The API in four groups:

1. **The stock and the books learn the new documents:** a move out may name its value, the stock books write a
   purchase return, and the purchase books write a debit note and a supplier refund.
2. **17b's and 17c's documents learn what went back:** goods receipts report it, bills bill only what was kept and
   report what debit notes took off, supplier payments count refunds and share their allocation check.
3. **The three new services:** purchase returns, debit notes, supplier refunds.
4. **The controllers, the module,** and the suppliers and accounts the new documents hold on to.

Every new service is the 15d service of the same name seen from the other side: `SalesReturnsService` →
`PurchaseReturnsService`, `CreditNotesService` → `DebitNotesService`, `RefundsService` → `SupplierRefundsService`.
The notes below say where they differ. Decisions 32–37 came up while building this part.

### A move out may name its value: `inventory/stock-posting.service.ts`


- **Until now a move out never took a value from its caller.** Step 14 made the stock posting the one place that
  knows what stock is worth, so a delivery or a transfer always left at the average. A purchase return is the first
  move out that must leave at another cost: the receipt line's (decision 2). Without that, goods received not billed
  would not be put back exactly, and the debit note could never clear it.
- **`outflowAt()` keeps step 14's two promises** (decision 32). Taking all the stock takes all its value, through
  `outflowValue()`, so zero stock is worth zero. Taking part never takes more than the stock is worth, so what stays
  is never worth less than nothing. In between, the named value is taken, and the moving average of what stays is
  worked out again by `apply()`, as before.
- **With no stock to go by** (the workspace allows negative stock), the named value is taken as it is: there is no
  value to protect.
- **The value it really took comes back to the caller,** as for every move (`post()` returns them). The return
  compares it with the receipt's cost and books any difference.

- **Only a few sources may post to the stock accounts** (17c): stock documents, a bill, a reversal and the year-end
  close. A debit note joins them: it credits Goods received not billed with what a purchase return put back on it
  (decision 1). A purchase return is a stock source already (17d.1). A manual entry still may not touch the account,
  which is why decision 9 needs the debit note without a bill.

- **The sales return of 15d turned round:** Dr Goods received not billed, Cr Inventory. The debit takes each line's
  receipt warehouse's branch, because that is where the receipt credited it (17b), and the account must clear branch by
  branch. The credit takes the return warehouse's branch: the goods leave there, even if they were moved since.
- **`value` and `moved` are two numbers** because of decision 32: what goes on goods received not billed (the
  receipt's cost) and what the stock gave up. They differ only at the edges; the difference goes to the account the
  caller names. The caller looks that account up only when they differ, so a workspace that never chose a price
  difference account can still post an ordinary return. Passing none when they differ is a bug, not a user mistake,
  so it throws.
- **It stays in the inventory module.** `purchase_return` is a stock journal source (17d.1, decision 12), like the goods
  receipt's, and the price difference account comes in as an id, so the inventory module still knows nothing of
  purchasing.


- **`debitNote()` is the bill's entry the other way round** (decision 1). Each goods line credits goods received not
  billed with what its return put there, with that branch, and the rest of its net goes to the price difference
  (decision 22). The line can be a debit or a credit: a bill cheaper than the order leaves a negative difference.
  `summed()` turns each sum into the right side, as for a bill.
- **`billAccounts()` takes what is needed, not the bill's lines.** A price cut on a bill of goods names no return line,
  so it needs no goods received not billed account; before, any goods line asked for one, and a workspace without it
  could not post a price cut.
- **`refund()` is the payment's entry the other way round:** Dr the money account, Cr Accounts payable with the
  supplier. The payable goes back up by what the debit note or the advance had taken off it.
- **`priceDifferenceAccountId()`** is the bill's lookup (Settings → Purchase, else Cost of goods sold) made public,
  for the purchase return's difference (decision 32).

- **`hasLineToBill` counts what was kept** (decision 17): a line whose goods all went back before a bill has nothing
  to bill and leaves the bill form's list. It is the condition of 17d.2's partial index, so the index is used.
- **`returnState` and `returnable`** are 15d's challan words and filter, with one difference: a line that turned
  everything back at the gate kept nothing, so it can never be "returnable" and does not hold a receipt at "partly
  returned".
- **`returns` lists posted returns only.** A draft sent nothing back yet; the receipt's page would otherwise show a
  return that may still be deleted.


- **A receipt line is billed for `keptQuantity()`** (decision 17): the check, its error and the "nothing to bill" case
  all read the kept quantity. A return posted after the draft was saved makes the stored line too big; the posting's
  recheck refuses it (`bill_receipt_line_quantity`), and so does the database (decision 29).
- **What the receipt booked, less what went back** (decision 37). The bill debits goods received not billed with the
  receipt line's value less what pre-bill returns credited back. `returnedBeforeBilling()` finds those returns: a
  posted return line of the receipt line with no bill line (decision 28 sets the bill line exactly when one billed
  it). At posting it is read under the receipt lines' lock, which a return takes too (decision 34).
- **`isOpen` and the "paid" filter** count debit notes: a bill a debit note settled is not open, and is paid.
- **`read()`:** each line and expense sends `debited`; the bill sends its posted debit notes and, while it owes, the
  supplier's open debit notes next to the advances (decision 24). `openDebitNotesOf()` is the advances' query with
  the debit note's columns, on 17d.2's `debit_notes_unapplied_idx`; its bill is read through an alias, because this
  query already reads `bills` for the page's own bill. The advances now leave out what refunds took back.

- **`allocate()` applies only what refunds left** (`amount − refunded`), like 15d's receipt.
- **`void()` refuses a payment with a refund** (`payment_has_refunds`): voiding it would undo money that is already back
  in the bank. The check reads `refunded` under the payment's lock, which a refund takes too (`lockSource()` below), so
  the two take turns. `supplier_payments_amount_check` is the last word and gets the same answer.
- **`checkBillAllocations()` is exported, with its error codes** (decision 36), and counts `amountDebited` in what a
  bill still owes. `paymentRace()` says "a payment or a debit note", because either can settle a bill's last taka.

### Purchase returns: `purchase/purchase-returns.service.ts` (new)

```ts
import { Inject, Injectable } from '@nestjs/common';
import {
  compareMoney,
  compareQuantity,
  keptQuantity,
  type PartyRef,
  prorateMoney,
  type PurchaseReturn,
  type PurchaseReturnInput,
  type PurchaseReturnSummary,
  type StockDocumentStatus,
  subtractMoney,
  sumQuantity,
  type UpdatePurchaseReturnInput,
} from '@omnivo/contracts';
import {
  billLines,
  bills,
  debitNoteLines,
  debitNotes,
  goodsReceiptLines,
  goodsReceipts,
  parties,
  purchaseOrderLines,
  purchaseOrders,
  purchaseReturnLines,
  purchaseReturns,
  stockValues,
  warehouses,
} from '@omnivo/db';
import { and, asc, desc, eq, inArray, type SQL, sql } from 'drizzle-orm';
import { z } from 'zod';

import { audit, created, diff } from '../common/audit/audit.js';
import { isCheckViolation } from '../common/db/pg-errors.js';
import { AppError, notFound, versionConflict } from '../common/http/app-error.js';
import { decodeCursor, toPage } from '../common/pagination/cursor.js';
import { currentPrincipal, getTenantId } from '../common/tenant/tenant-context.js';
import type { Transaction, WithTenant } from '../common/tenant/with-tenant.js';
import { WITH_TENANT } from '../infra/tokens.js';
import {
  assertWarehousesActive,
  batchesOf,
  type LineIssue,
  linePath,
  linesError,
  loadVariants,
  type ResolvedLine,
  resolveLines,
  toStockLine,
} from '../inventory/stock-lines.js';
import { StockBooksService } from '../inventory/stock-books.service.js';
import { StockPostingService } from '../inventory/stock-posting.service.js';
import { ValueAccess } from '../inventory/value-access.js';
import { NumberingService } from '../numbering/numbering.service.js';
import { customerRefs } from '../sales/sales-lines.js';
import { PurchaseBooksService } from './purchase-books.service.js';
import { assertSupplier } from './purchase-lines.js';

type ReturnRow = typeof purchaseReturns.$inferSelect;
type LineRow = typeof purchaseReturnLines.$inferSelect;

const cursorSchema = z.tuple([z.iso.date(), z.uuid()]);

// By the table's name: inside this subquery a bare "id" would be the line's own
const lineCount = sql<number>`(
  SELECT count(*)::int FROM purchase_return_lines l
   WHERE l.tenant_id = purchase_returns.tenant_id AND l.return_id = purchase_returns.id
)`;

// What a line names, as the form sends it and as the database keeps it
interface LineRefs {
  receiptLineId: string | null;
  variantId: string;
  unitId: string;
  quantity: string;
  batchId: string | null;
  serialNumbers: readonly string[];
}

// A goods receipt line a return line sends back from, with what its receipt says about it
interface ReceiptLine {
  id: string;
  supplierId: string;
  status: StockDocumentStatus;
  // The warehouse the goods came into: its branch booked goods received not billed (17b), so the
  // return puts their cost back there
  warehouseId: string;
  variantId: string;
  baseQuantity: string;
  returnedQuantity: string;
  batchId: string | null;
  serialNumbers: string[];
  value: string | null;
  billed: boolean;
  orderLineId: string | null;
}

// The lines once checked: resolved like a stock document's (the batch of a receipt line is the
// receipt line's), with the receipt lines they name
interface Checked {
  lines: ResolvedLine[];
  receipts: Map<string, ReceiptLine>;
}

// The bill line that billed a receipt line, and its bill
interface Billing {
  billId: string;
  billLineId: string;
}

function notDraft(): AppError {
  return new AppError(
    409,
    'stock_not_draft',
    'Only a draft can be changed. A posted return is final: goods that come again come on a goods receipt.',
  );
}

function toSummary(row: ReturnRow, supplier: PartyRef, lines: number): PurchaseReturnSummary {
  return {
    id: row.id,
    number: row.number,
    date: row.date,
    supplier,
    warehouseId: row.warehouseId,
    reason: row.reason,
    status: row.status,
    note: row.note,
    lineCount: lines,
    postedAt: row.postedAt?.toISOString() ?? null,
    version: row.version,
    updatedAt: row.updatedAt.toISOString(),
  };
}

// What `quantity` going back from a receipt line puts back on goods received not billed: its share
// of what the receipt line came in at (decision 2). Counted over everything sent back from the line
// so far, so a line that goes back in three goes gives back exactly its value, with no paisa left
// over by rounding.
function returnValue(receipt: ReceiptLine, quantity: string): string {
  if (receipt.value === null) throw new Error(`Posted receipt line ${receipt.id} has no value`);
  const after = sumQuantity([receipt.returnedQuantity, quantity]);
  return subtractMoney(
    prorateMoney(receipt.value, after, receipt.baseQuantity),
    prorateMoney(receipt.value, receipt.returnedQuantity, receipt.baseQuantity),
  );
}

// The database's last word on a receipt line (goods_receipt_lines_returned_check: never more back
// than was accepted), and on a bill and a return of the same goods posted at the same moment
// (purchase_returns_receipts_check, decision 28). The locks in postAndLog() make both unreachable in
// practice; each still answers with the code the form knows.
function returnRace(error: unknown): unknown {
  if (isCheckViolation(error, 'goods_receipt_lines_returned_check')) {
    return new AppError(
      409,
      'purchase_return_over_received',
      'Another return sent some of these goods back first. Reload and try again.',
    );
  }
  if (isCheckViolation(error, 'purchase_returns_receipts_check')) {
    return new AppError(
      409,
      'purchase_return_receipt_line_invalid',
      'A bill billed some of these goods while the return was posted. Reload and try again.',
    );
  }
  return error;
}

// Purchase returns (step 17d): goods sent back to a supplier, out of the warehouse the return names.
// A draft is changed freely; "Post" numbers it, takes the stock out at the cost it came in at, puts
// that cost back on goods received not billed, and counts it on the receipt lines it names (and,
// before a bill billed them, on the order's lines). It moves no money: a debit note does that.
@Injectable()
export class PurchaseReturnsService {
  constructor(
    @Inject(WITH_TENANT) private readonly withTenant: WithTenant,
    private readonly numbering: NumberingService,
    private readonly posting: StockPostingService,
    private readonly books: StockBooksService,
    private readonly purchaseBooks: PurchaseBooksService,
    private readonly access: ValueAccess,
  ) {}

  list(query: {
    limit: number;
    cursor?: string | undefined;
    status?: StockDocumentStatus | undefined;
    supplierId?: string | undefined;
    warehouseId?: string | undefined;
  }): Promise<{ items: PurchaseReturnSummary[]; nextCursor: string | null }> {
    const after = decodeCursor(query.cursor, cursorSchema);
    return this.withTenant(async (tx) => {
      const rows = await this.rows(
        tx,
        and(
          query.status === undefined ? undefined : eq(purchaseReturns.status, query.status),
          query.supplierId === undefined
            ? undefined
            : eq(purchaseReturns.supplierId, query.supplierId),
          query.warehouseId === undefined
            ? undefined
            : eq(purchaseReturns.warehouseId, query.warehouseId),
          after === undefined
            ? undefined
            : sql`(${purchaseReturns.date}, ${purchaseReturns.id}) < (${after[0]}::date, ${after[1]}::uuid)`,
        ),
        query.limit + 1,
      );
      const page = toPage(rows, query.limit, (last) => [
        last.purchaseReturn.date,
        last.purchaseReturn.id,
      ]);
      return {
        items: page.items.map((row) => toSummary(row.purchaseReturn, row.supplier, row.lineCount)),
        nextCursor: page.nextCursor,
      };
    });
  }

  get(id: string): Promise<PurchaseReturn> {
    return this.withTenant((tx) => this.read(tx, id));
  }

  async create(input: PurchaseReturnInput): Promise<PurchaseReturn> {
    try {
      return await this.withTenant(async (tx) => {
        const supplier = await assertSupplier(tx, input.supplierId);
        await assertWarehousesActive(tx, [
          { field: 'warehouseId', warehouseId: input.warehouseId },
        ]);
        const checked = await this.checkLines(tx, supplier.id, input.lines, false);
        const [row] = await tx
          .insert(purchaseReturns)
          .values({
            tenantId: getTenantId(),
            date: input.date,
            supplierId: supplier.id,
            warehouseId: input.warehouseId,
            reason: input.reason,
            note: input.note,
            createdBy: currentPrincipal().userId,
            updatedBy: currentPrincipal().userId,
          })
          .returning();
        if (!row) throw new Error('Purchase return insert returned no row');
        await this.writeLines(tx, row.id, input.lines, checked.lines);
        await audit(tx, {
          action: 'purchase_return.created',
          entityType: 'purchase_return',
          entityId: row.id,
          changes: created(await this.snapshot(tx, row, supplier, checked.lines.length)),
        });
        if (input.post) await this.postAndLog(tx, row);
        return this.read(tx, row.id);
      });
    } catch (error) {
      throw returnRace(error);
    }
  }

  async update(id: string, input: UpdatePurchaseReturnInput): Promise<PurchaseReturn> {
    try {
      return await this.withTenant(async (tx) => {
        const before = await this.lockDraft(tx, id, input.version);
        const linesBefore = await this.linesOf(tx, id);
        const supplierBefore = await this.supplierOf(tx, before.supplierId);
        const supplier = await assertSupplier(tx, input.supplierId, before.supplierId);
        await assertWarehousesActive(tx, [
          { field: 'warehouseId', warehouseId: input.warehouseId },
        ]);
        const checked = await this.checkLines(tx, supplier.id, input.lines, false);
        const [updated] = await tx
          .update(purchaseReturns)
          .set({
            date: input.date,
            supplierId: supplier.id,
            warehouseId: input.warehouseId,
            reason: input.reason,
            note: input.note,
            version: sql`${purchaseReturns.version} + 1`,
            updatedBy: currentPrincipal().userId,
          })
          .where(and(eq(purchaseReturns.tenantId, getTenantId()), eq(purchaseReturns.id, id)))
          .returning();
        if (!updated) throw notFound('Purchase return');
        await this.writeLines(tx, id, input.lines, checked.lines);
        await audit(tx, {
          action: 'purchase_return.updated',
          entityType: 'purchase_return',
          entityId: id,
          changes: diff(
            await this.snapshot(tx, before, supplierBefore, linesBefore.length),
            await this.snapshot(tx, updated, supplier, checked.lines.length),
          ),
        });
        if (input.post) await this.postAndLog(tx, updated);
        return this.read(tx, id);
      });
    } catch (error) {
      throw returnRace(error);
    }
  }

  remove(id: string, version: number): Promise<void> {
    return this.withTenant(async (tx) => {
      const before = await this.lockDraft(tx, id, version);
      const lines = await this.linesOf(tx, id);
      const supplier = await this.supplierOf(tx, before.supplierId);
      // The lines go with it (ON DELETE CASCADE). A draft sent nothing back: nothing to undo.
      await tx
        .delete(purchaseReturns)
        .where(and(eq(purchaseReturns.tenantId, getTenantId()), eq(purchaseReturns.id, id)));
      const snapshot = await this.snapshot(tx, before, supplier, lines.length);
      await audit(tx, {
        action: 'purchase_return.deleted',
        entityType: 'purchase_return',
        entityId: id,
        changes: diff(
          snapshot,
          Object.fromEntries(Object.keys(snapshot).map((field) => [field, null])),
        ),
      });
    });
  }

  async post(id: string, version: number): Promise<PurchaseReturn> {
    try {
      return await this.withTenant(async (tx) => {
        const draft = await this.lockDraft(tx, id, version);
        await this.postAndLog(tx, draft);
        return this.read(tx, id);
      });
    } catch (error) {
      throw returnRace(error);
    }
  }

  // Every rule of a line the contract cannot check. A line from a receipt line: a line of a posted
  // goods receipt of this supplier, of the same item (in any of its units), with its batch, no more
  // than it kept (accepted less what went back already; what was turned back at the gate never came
  // in, decision 16), and only serial numbers that came in on it (decision 15). A line on its own:
  // an item of this workspace with an existing batch, like a stock line that goes out
  // (resolveLines in 'out' mode: an archived item can still go back), and an average cost to leave
  // at. All problems at once, under each line. lock: true when posting (the receipt lines are
  // locked, see receiptLines()).
  private async checkLines(
    tx: Transaction,
    supplierId: string,
    lines: readonly LineRefs[],
    lock: boolean,
  ): Promise<Checked> {
    const receipts = await this.receiptLines(
      tx,
      lines.flatMap((line) => (line.receiptLineId === null ? [] : [line.receiptLineId])),
      lock,
    );
    const receiptOf = (line: LineRefs) =>
      line.receiptLineId === null ? undefined : receipts.get(line.receiptLineId);

    const issues: LineIssue[] = [];
    lines.forEach((line, index) => {
      if (line.receiptLineId === null) return;
      const receipt = receiptOf(line);
      if (
        receipt?.supplierId !== supplierId ||
        receipt.status !== 'posted' ||
        receipt.variantId !== line.variantId
      ) {
        issues.push({
          path: linePath(index, 'receiptLineId'),
          code: 'purchase_return_receipt_line_invalid',
        });
      }
    });
    if (issues.length > 0) throw linesError(issues);

    // A receipt line's goods go back in its own batch: the form sends none (the contract refuses
    // one), and a stored draft line keeps the one written when it was saved
    const resolved = await resolveLines(
      tx,
      lines.map((line) => ({
        variantId: line.variantId,
        unitId: line.unitId,
        quantity: line.quantity,
        batchId: receiptOf(line)?.batchId ?? line.batchId,
        serialNumbers: [...line.serialNumbers],
      })),
      'out',
      { lock },
    );

    resolved.forEach((line, index) => {
      const typed = lines[index];
      const receipt = typed === undefined ? undefined : receiptOf(typed);
      if (receipt === undefined) return;
      if (compareQuantity(line.baseQuantity, keptQuantity(receipt)) > 0) {
        issues.push({ path: linePath(index, 'quantity'), code: 'purchase_return_over_received' });
      }
      const came = new Set(receipt.serialNumbers);
      if (line.serialNumbers.some((serial) => !came.has(serial))) {
        issues.push({
          path: linePath(index, 'serialNumbers'),
          code: 'purchase_return_serial_invalid',
        });
      }
    });
    // A line on its own leaves at the average cost (decision 2): an item that never had a cost
    // (no stock ever came in) has nothing to leave at
    const costed = await this.costedVariants(
      tx,
      lines.flatMap((line) => (line.receiptLineId === null ? [line.variantId] : [])),
    );
    lines.forEach((line, index) => {
      if (line.receiptLineId === null && !costed.has(line.variantId)) {
        issues.push({ path: linePath(index, 'variantId'), code: 'purchase_return_cost_unknown' });
      }
    });
    if (issues.length > 0) throw linesError(issues);
    return { lines: resolved, receipts };
  }

  // The variants among `ids` that have an average cost (step 14's stock_values row)
  private async costedVariants(tx: Transaction, ids: readonly string[]): Promise<Set<string>> {
    if (ids.length === 0) return new Set();
    const rows = await tx
      .select({ variantId: stockValues.variantId })
      .from(stockValues)
      .where(
        and(
          eq(stockValues.tenantId, getTenantId()),
          inArray(stockValues.variantId, [...new Set(ids)]),
          sql`${stockValues.unitCost} IS NOT NULL`,
        ),
      );
    return new Set(rows.map((row) => row.variantId));
  }

  // The goods receipt lines some return lines name, with their receipt's supplier, status and
  // warehouse. lock: the lines are locked FOR NO KEY UPDATE in id order, then read, so
  // returned_quantity and billed are what the last posting committed. A bill's posting locks the
  // same lines the same way (BillsService.receiptLines), so a return and a bill of one receipt line
  // take turns: whichever is second sees the first. NO KEY: a draft line being saved against them
  // (a KEY SHARE lock through its foreign key) is not blocked.
  private async receiptLines(
    tx: Transaction,
    ids: readonly string[],
    lock: boolean,
  ): Promise<Map<string, ReceiptLine>> {
    if (ids.length === 0) return new Map();
    const query = tx
      .select({
        id: goodsReceiptLines.id,
        variantId: goodsReceiptLines.variantId,
        baseQuantity: goodsReceiptLines.baseQuantity,
        returnedQuantity: goodsReceiptLines.returnedQuantity,
        batchId: goodsReceiptLines.batchId,
        serialNumbers: goodsReceiptLines.serialNumbers,
        value: goodsReceiptLines.value,
        billed: goodsReceiptLines.billed,
        orderLineId: goodsReceiptLines.orderLineId,
        supplierId: goodsReceipts.supplierId,
        status: goodsReceipts.status,
        warehouseId: goodsReceipts.warehouseId,
      })
      .from(goodsReceiptLines)
      .innerJoin(
        goodsReceipts,
        and(
          eq(goodsReceipts.tenantId, goodsReceiptLines.tenantId),
          eq(goodsReceipts.id, goodsReceiptLines.receiptId),
        ),
      )
      .where(
        and(
          eq(goodsReceiptLines.tenantId, getTenantId()),
          inArray(goodsReceiptLines.id, [...new Set(ids)]),
        ),
      )
      .orderBy(asc(goodsReceiptLines.id));
    const rows = lock ? await query.for('no key update', { of: goodsReceiptLines }) : await query;
    return new Map(rows.map((row) => [row.id, row]));
  }

  // Posting, in the caller's transaction, in the order migration 0042 needs: the lines are written
  // while the return is still a draft (their values, and the bill line of a billed receipt line),
  // then the receipt lines and the orders, and the return becomes posted last. A refused step
  // leaves nothing: no number used, no stock moved.
  private async postAndLog(tx: Transaction, draft: ReturnRow): Promise<void> {
    const tenantId = getTenantId();
```
