```ts
describe("another workspace's purchase returns", () => {
  it('are not read, changed, posted or deleted', async () => {
    for (const back of [returnOfB, draftReturnOfB]) {
      const answers = await Promise.all([
        as(tenantA, 'GET', `/purchase-returns/${back.id}`),
        as(tenantA, 'PUT', `/purchase-returns/${back.id}`, {
          ...returnForm(supplierOfA.id, warehouseOfA, [
            returnLine(variantOf(productOfA), pcsOf(unitsOfA)),
          ]),
          version: back.version,
        }),
        as(tenantA, 'POST', `/purchase-returns/${back.id}/post`, { version: back.version }),
        as(tenantA, 'DELETE', `/purchase-returns/${back.id}?version=${String(back.version)}`),
      ]);
      expect(answers.map((res) => res.statusCode)).toEqual([404, 404, 404, 404]);
      const after = await returnOfBNow(back.id);
      expect([after.status, after.version]).toEqual([back.status, back.version]);
    }
    const page = purchaseReturnPageSchema.parse(
      (await as(tenantA, 'GET', '/purchase-returns')).json(),
    );
    expect(page.items).toEqual([]);
  });

  it("send back none of B's receipt lines, from none of B's stores, to none of B's suppliers", async () => {
    const line = await as(
      tenantA,
      'POST',
      '/purchase-returns',
      returnForm(supplierOfA.id, warehouseOfA, [
        returnLine(variantOf(productOfA), pcsOf(unitsOfA), {
          receiptLineId: receiptOfB.lines[0]?.id ?? '',
        }),
      ]),
    );
    expect(problemOf(line).fieldErrors).toEqual({
      'lines.0.receiptLineId': ['purchase_return_receipt_line_invalid'],
    });
    const store = await as(
      tenantA,
      'POST',
      '/purchase-returns',
      returnForm(supplierOfA.id, warehouseOfB, [
        returnLine(variantOf(productOfA), pcsOf(unitsOfA)),
      ]),
    );
    expect(problemOf(store).fieldErrors).toEqual({ warehouseId: ['stock_warehouse_invalid'] });
    const supplier = await as(
      tenantA,
      'POST',
      '/purchase-returns',
      returnForm(supplierOfB.id, warehouseOfA, [
        returnLine(variantOf(productOfA), pcsOf(unitsOfA)),
      ]),
    );
    expect(problemOf(supplier).fieldErrors).toEqual({ supplierId: ['purchase_supplier_invalid'] });
    // B's goods receipt counts only B's return
    const receipt = goodsReceiptSchema.parse(
      (await as(tenantB, 'GET', `/goods-receipts/${receiptOfB.id}`)).json(),
    );
    expect(receipt.lines[0]?.returnedQuantity).toBe('10.0000');
  });
});

describe("another workspace's debit notes", () => {
  it('are not read, changed, posted, deleted or applied', async () => {
    for (const note of [noteOfB, draftNoteOfB]) {
      const version = { version: note.version };
      const answers = await Promise.all([
        as(tenantA, 'GET', `/debit-notes/${note.id}`),
        as(tenantA, 'PUT', `/debit-notes/${note.id}`, {
          ...debitForm(supplierOfA.id, {
            branchId: warehouseOfA.branchId,
            // A valid form, so the answer is about whose debit note it is
            lines: [
              debitLine(pcsOf(unitsOfA), { returnLineId: note.id, taxRateId: vatOf(ratesOfA) }),
            ],
          }),
          version: note.version,
        }),
        as(tenantA, 'POST', `/debit-notes/${note.id}/post`, version),
        as(tenantA, 'DELETE', `/debit-notes/${note.id}?version=${String(note.version)}`),
        as(tenantA, 'PUT', `/debit-notes/${note.id}/allocations`, { ...version, allocations: [] }),
      ]);
      expect(answers.map((res) => res.statusCode)).toEqual([404, 404, 404, 404, 404]);
      const after = await noteOfBNow(note.id);
      expect([after.status, after.version, after.applied]).toEqual([
        note.status,
        note.version,
        note.applied,
      ]);
    }
    const page = debitNotePageSchema.parse((await as(tenantA, 'GET', '/debit-notes')).json());
    expect(page.items).toEqual([]);
    const byBill = debitNotePageSchema.parse(
      (await as(tenantA, 'GET', `/debit-notes?billId=${billOfB.id}`)).json(),
    );
    expect(byBill.items).toEqual([]);
  });

  it("take nothing off B's bills, bill lines, expenses or return lines, nor with B's VAT rates", async () => {
    const bill = await as(
      tenantA,
      'POST',
      '/debit-notes',
      debitForm(supplierOfA.id, {
        billId: billOfB.id,
        lines: [debitLine(pcsOf(unitsOfA), { billLineId: billOfB.lines[0]?.id ?? '' })],
      }),
    );
    expect(problemOf(bill).fieldErrors).toEqual({ billId: ['debit_note_bill_invalid'] });
    // Without a bill: B's return line, at B's VAT rate, at B's branch
    const returnLineOfB = returnOfB.lines[0]?.id ?? '';
    const own = await as(
      tenantA,
      'POST',
      '/debit-notes',
      debitForm(supplierOfA.id, {
        branchId: warehouseOfA.branchId,
        lines: [
          debitLine(pcsOf(unitsOfA), { returnLineId: returnLineOfB, taxRateId: vatOf(ratesOfA) }),
        ],
      }),
    );
    expect(problemOf(own).fieldErrors).toEqual({
      'lines.0.returnLineId': ['debit_note_return_invalid'],
    });
    // A's own return of yarn from before Omnivo, debited at B's rate, or at B's branch
    const ownBack = await as(
      tenantA,
      'POST',
      '/purchase-returns',
      returnForm(
        supplierOfA.id,
        warehouseOfA,
        [returnLine(variantOf(productOfA), pcsOf(unitsOfA), { quantity: '2' })],
        { post: true },
      ),
    );
    expect(ownBack.statusCode, ownBack.body).toBe(201);
    const lineOfA = purchaseReturnSchema.parse(ownBack.json()).lines[0]?.id ?? '';
    const rate = await as(
      tenantA,
      'POST',
      '/debit-notes',
      debitForm(supplierOfA.id, {
        branchId: warehouseOfA.branchId,
        lines: [debitLine(pcsOf(unitsOfA), { returnLineId: lineOfA, taxRateId: vatOf(ratesOfB) })],
      }),
    );
    expect(problemOf(rate).fieldErrors).toEqual({ 'lines.0.taxRateId': ['tax_rate_invalid'] });
    const branch = await as(
      tenantA,
      'POST',
      '/debit-notes',
      debitForm(supplierOfA.id, {
        branchId: warehouseOfB.branchId,
        lines: [debitLine(pcsOf(unitsOfA), { returnLineId: lineOfA, taxRateId: vatOf(ratesOfA) })],
      }),
    );
    expect(problemOf(branch).fieldErrors).toEqual({ branchId: ['purchase_branch_invalid'] });
    // B's bill as where A's debit note's money goes
    const note = await as(
      tenantA,
      'POST',
      '/debit-notes',
      debitForm(supplierOfA.id, {
        branchId: warehouseOfA.branchId,
        lines: [debitLine(pcsOf(unitsOfA), { returnLineId: lineOfA, taxRateId: vatOf(ratesOfA) })],
        post: true,
      }),
    );
    expect(note.statusCode, note.body).toBe(201);
    const noteOfA = debitNoteSchema.parse(note.json());
    const applied = await as(tenantA, 'PUT', `/debit-notes/${noteOfA.id}/allocations`, {
      version: noteOfA.version,
      allocations: [{ billId: billOfB.id, amount: '100' }],
    });
    expect(problemOf(applied).fieldErrors).toEqual({
      'allocations.0.billId': ['debit_note_allocation_invalid'],
    });
    // B's bill and return line count only B's debit note
    const billNow = billSchema.parse((await as(tenantB, 'GET', `/bills/${billOfB.id}`)).json());
    expect([billNow.amountDebited, billNow.lines[0]?.debited]).toEqual(['2875.0000', '2875.0000']);
    expect((await returnOfBNow(returnOfB.id)).lines[0]?.debitedQuantity).toBe('10.0000');
    // Nor B's expense, on a bill of A's own
    const billOfA = await as(tenantA, 'POST', '/bills', {
      supplierId: supplierOfA.id,
      date: '2026-10-16',
      dueDate: '',
      supplierBillNumber: 'GYH-0412',
      mushakNumber: '',
      mushakDate: '',
      branchId: warehouseOfA.branchId,
      warehouseId: '',
      pricesIncludeVat: false,
      note: '',
      lines: [],
      expenses: [
        {
          accountId: codeIn(accountsOfA, '5270'),
          description: 'Linking machine repair',
          amount: '1000',
          taxRateId: vatOf(ratesOfA),
        },
      ],
      submit: true,
    });
    expect(billOfA.statusCode, billOfA.body).toBe(201);
    const expense = await as(
      tenantA,
      'POST',
      '/debit-notes',
      debitForm(supplierOfA.id, {
        billId: billSchema.parse(billOfA.json()).id,
        expenses: [{ billExpenseId: billOfB.expenses[0]?.id ?? '', amount: '100' }],
      }),
    );
    expect(problemOf(expense).fieldErrors).toEqual({
      'expenses.0.billExpenseId': ['debit_note_expense_invalid'],
    });
  });
});

describe("another workspace's supplier refunds", () => {
  it('are not read or voided', async () => {
    const answers = await Promise.all([
      as(tenantA, 'GET', `/supplier-refunds/${refundOfB.id}`),
      as(tenantA, 'POST', `/supplier-refunds/${refundOfB.id}/void`, {
        version: refundOfB.version,
        date: '2026-10-18',
        reason: 'Cheque bounced',
      }),
    ]);
    expect(answers.map((res) => res.statusCode)).toEqual([404, 404]);
    const after = supplierRefundSchema.parse(
      (await as(tenantB, 'GET', `/supplier-refunds/${refundOfB.id}`)).json(),
    );
    expect([after.status, after.version]).toEqual(['posted', refundOfB.version]);
    const page = supplierRefundPageSchema.parse(
      (await as(tenantA, 'GET', '/supplier-refunds')).json(),
    );
    expect(page.items).toEqual([]);
  });

  it("pay back none of B's debit notes or payments, nor into B's money", async () => {
    const note = await as(
      tenantA,
      'POST',
      '/supplier-refunds',
      refundForm(supplierOfA.id, warehouseOfA, accountsOfA, { debitNoteId: noteOfB.id }),
    );
    expect(problemOf(note).fieldErrors).toEqual({
      debitNoteId: ['supplier_refund_source_invalid'],
    });
    const payment = await as(
      tenantA,
      'POST',
      '/supplier-refunds',
      refundForm(supplierOfA.id, warehouseOfA, accountsOfA, { paymentId: advanceOfB.id }),
    );
    expect(problemOf(payment).fieldErrors).toEqual({
      paymentId: ['supplier_refund_source_invalid'],
    });
    // A's own debit note, into B's cash, at B's branch
    const [noteOfA] = debitNotePageSchema.parse(
      (await as(tenantA, 'GET', '/debit-notes?status=posted')).json(),
    ).items;
    const money = await as(
      tenantA,
      'POST',
      '/supplier-refunds',
      refundForm(supplierOfA.id, warehouseOfA, accountsOfB, { debitNoteId: noteOfA?.id ?? '' }),
    );
    expect(problemOf(money).fieldErrors).toEqual({
      accountId: ['supplier_refund_account_invalid'],
    });
    const branch = await as(
      tenantA,
      'POST',
      '/supplier-refunds',
      refundForm(supplierOfA.id, warehouseOfB, accountsOfA, { debitNoteId: noteOfA?.id ?? '' }),
    );
    expect(problemOf(branch).fieldErrors).toEqual({ branchId: ['purchase_branch_invalid'] });
    // B's money is only what B's refund moved
    const advance = supplierPaymentSchema.parse(
      (await as(tenantB, 'GET', `/supplier-payments/${advanceOfB.id}`)).json(),
    );
    expect(advance.refunded).toBe('1000.0000');
    expect((await noteOfBNow(noteOfB.id)).refunded).toBe('0.0000');
  });
});
```

- **B has one of everything:** a received and billed order, a posted return after the bill and a draft one, a posted
  debit note applied to the bill and a draft one, an advance and a refund from it. A has its own yarn from before
  Omnivo, so its own return and debit note are real and only B's ids are wrong.
- **Every route of B's documents answers 404** to A, and B's document is unchanged afterwards (status, version,
  money). Each body A sends is a valid form, so the 404 is about whose document it is, not a 400 about the form.
- **Every id of B's that A names is "pick one from the list":** B's receipt line, store, supplier, bill, return line,
  VAT rate, branch, expense, debit note, payment and money account, each under its own field. B's documents still
  count only B's own returns, debits and refunds.
- The seven new tables are also in the RLS coverage test (`rls-coverage.tenant-leak.int.spec.ts`), which finds every
  table with a `tenant_id` and checks that its row security is on: it needed no change.

- **23 series now, not 20,** and the three new ones are checked by name: PRN, DN and SRF, each by fiscal year. The
  list comes from the contract (17d.1), so a series missing from the database's seed would show here.

### Check this part

```bash
pnpm --filter @omnivo/api typecheck
npx eslint apps/api/src/purchase
cd apps/api
npx vitest run purchase-returns --maxWorkers=3
pnpm test:integration
pnpm test:tenant-leak
```

The two new files pass (25 and 6 tests), three runs in a row, and so does every older integration and tenant-leak
suite of the API (52 files, 579 tests).

> **What we checked.** All of the above on a real database, plus the two "break it on purpose" checks described at
> the top of this part. The app and the mock still do not type-check: they learn the new words in 17d.5 and the
> screens in 17d.6.

---

## 17d.5 — `packages/i18n`: the words

The screens of 17d.6 need their words in English and Bangla, and the app cannot type-check without them, so they
come first. This part changes only the two locale files. The ui package needs nothing new: the return form is built
from the stock line rows (step 13), the debit note from the sales line editor and the bill's expenses card (17c), the
money parts from the allocation table (15c), and the printed pages from `PrintSheet` (15c).

When this part starts, `packages/i18n` has one error: the `errors` object is missing the 32 new codes of 17d.1. When
it ends, the i18n package compiles, and the app has 13 type errors left. None of them is about a word: they are the
new fields of 17d.1 that the screens and the mock server do not know yet (the bill pills do not pass
`amountDebited`, the bill test fixture and the mock bills lack `amountDebited`, `debitNoteTotal`, `debitNotes`,
`openDebitNotes` and a line's `debited`, the mock payments lack `refunded`, and the mock goods receipts lack
`returnedQuantity`, `returnState` and `returns`). 17d.6 fixes the screens, 17d.7 the mocks.

- **New keys go into `en.ts` first** (CLAUDE.md → Language). `bn.ts` has the type `Messages`, taken from `en`, so a
  key missing in Bangla fails the type check. The `errors` object ends with `satisfies Record<ErrorCode, string>`,
  so all 32 codes of 17d.1 must be here, or the package does not compile.
- **Keys built from contract values.** The numbering page calls `` t(`numbering.documents.${type}`) ``, the journal
  `` t(`journal.sources.${source}`) ``, the roles matrix `` t(`permissions.${key}`) ``, the audit log
  `` t(`audit.actions.${action}`) `` and `` t(`audit.entityTypes.${type}`) ``, and the stock card
  `` t(`stock.kinds.${kind}`) ``. These template strings are typed from the contract's unions, so the three number
  series (`purchase.return`, `purchase.debit_note`, `purchase.refund`), the three journal sources, the three
  permissions, the eleven audit actions, the three entity types and the movement kind `purchase_return` each need a
  key.
- **The new unions the pages show get a key for every member:** `goodsReceipts.returnStates`, `bills.debitStates`,
  `purchaseReturns.reasons`, `debitNotes.reasons`, `supplierRefunds.sources` and each document's `statuses`. That
  includes `none`, even though the pages show no pill for it, for the same reason as in 15d: a template string typed
  from the union needs every member.
- **`nav`:** "Purchase returns", "Debit notes" and "Supplier refunds" in the Purchase group, after Supplier payments.
  "Purchase returns", not "Returns": the Sales group already has "Sales returns", and a store keeper should never
  wonder which way the goods went. "Supplier refunds", not "Refunds", for the same reason: the Sales group has
  "Refunds", which is money the company pays out; this one is money that comes in.
- **`numbering` and `journal.sources`:** the names of PRN, DN and SRF (decision 10) and of the three sources. The
  Numbering page shows these names, so "Supplier refund" again says whose refund it is.
- **The journal hints.** The journal refuses to reverse an entry that a purchase document made
  (`journal_is_purchase`). In 17c, `billEntryHint` said only that the bill stays as it is, because there was no way
  back yet; now it says how to take money off it. `debitNoteEntryHint` and `supplierRefundEntryHint` follow the 15d
  hints of the credit note and the refund: a debit note is never undone, a refund is undone by voiding it. A purchase
  return needs no hint of its own: `purchase_return` is in `STOCK_JOURNAL_SOURCES` (17d.1), so the journal page
  already shows `stockEntryHint` for it.
- **`stock.kinds.purchase_return` is "Sent back".** It is the stock card's movement column, next to "Goods receipt"
  and the sales return's "Came back". "Returned" alone would not say which way.
- **`suppliers.inAdvance` is now "They owe you ৳…".** Before 17d, a supplier's balance went the other way only
  through an advance paid, so the text said "paid in advance". Now an unapplied debit note does the same (decision 4),
  and "paid in advance" would be wrong for a price cut. The key keeps its name, so `lib/suppliers.ts` does not
  change. The statement's empty text names the debit notes and refunds, which now post to the supplier's payable.
- **Goods receipts.** A posted receipt shows how much of it went back (`returnStates`) and lists the returns
  (`returnsTitle`), and each line says how much went back (`lineReturned`). `makeReturn` is the receipt page's button
  that opens a new return with the receipt's lines. It says "Send goods back", what the store keeper does.
- **Bills.**
  - `debitStates` is the pill that `debitStateOf()` (17d.1) works out; the page shows "Debited" in place of the payment
    pill when the whole total was taken off (decision 6), like "Credited" on an invoice.
  - `debited` is the row under "Paid", `lineDebited` the line under a bill line or an expense that a debit note took
    money off, and `debitNotesTitle` the list of the posted debit notes (the bill's `debitNotes`).
  - `writeDebitNote` opens a new debit note for this bill. `debitWhole` is the "Debit whole bill" button: it saves a
    draft from `wholeBillDebit()` and opens it, and `debitWholeDone` is the toast. It says the draft must be checked
    and posted, so nobody thinks the bill is debited already. It names the expenses too, because a whole debit
    takes them off as well.
  - `returnedBeforeBilling` is the line under a receipt line that partly went back before it was billed: the bill
    bills only `keptQuantity()`, and without the line the quantity would look wrong next to the receipt's.
  - `openDebitNotes*` is the second card next to "Advances to apply": the supplier's posted debit notes with money
    left (`openDebitNotes`). Like the advances, they are applied from their own page, where the money is, so the
    subtitle says so. `debitNoteNoBill` is for a debit note without a bill (decision 9), which has no bill number to
    show.
- **Supplier payments.** `refunded` is the "Paid back" row and `refund` the button that records the supplier paying
  the advance back. `unappliedNotice` now says that the advance can also come back as money.
- **Purchase returns** (built like `salesReturns`; the differences are on purpose):
  - `reasons` are the sales return's `RETURN_REASONS` (decision 13). `wrong_item` is "Wrong item sent": the
    supplier sent it.
  - `warehouse` is "Sent from warehouse", and `warehouseHint` says the box starts as the receipt's warehouse and may
    change if the goods were moved (decision 14). A return takes stock out, so the stock is checked in that
    warehouse.
  - Two ways to add a line. "Add from goods receipts" opens a picker of the supplier's posted receipts that can still
    send goods back (`GET /goods-receipts?return=returnable`); "Add items" (from `stockLines`) adds a line on its own.
    Under each line, `fromReceipt` and `leftToReturn` say where it comes from and how much can still go, so the person
    sees the limit before the server says `purchase_return_over_received`. `ownLine` says a line on its own leaves at
    the average cost (decision 2).
  - `postHint` says what posting books and what it does to the order (decision 3), and that it moves no money. The
    person who posts a return is often the store keeper; the hint tells them the accountant writes the debit note.
  - On its own page, each line says whether it was billed (`lineBilled`, `lineNotBilled`) and how much a debit note
    took off (`lineDebited`). `debitNotice` asks for a debit note when some goods were billed already or came from no
    receipt (decision 9), and `makeDebitNote` is its button.
- **Debit notes** (built like `creditNotes`; the differences are on purpose):
  - `reasons` are the credit note's (decision 13); `goods_returned` says "Goods sent back".
  - `bill*` is the bill box. `billOption` shows the supplier's own bill number next to ours, because the supplier's
    paper names theirs. `billNone` is the empty choice of decision 9, and `noBillHint` says what such a debit note
    debits and what the person must type, because without a bill there is no price to copy. `branch*` and
    `pricesIncludeVat*` show only without a bill; with one, the API takes the bill's (decision 19), so the form shows
    `branchFromBill`.
  - `supplierCredit*` is the Mushak 6.7 of decision 8, worded like the bill's Mushak 6.3: the number on the
    supplier's credit note, if they gave one.
  - Three ways to add a line: the bill's lines (a price cut is written the same way as on a credit note: keep the
    quantity, type the cut per unit), the returned goods (`returnPickerDescription` with a bill,
    `returnPickerOwnDescription` without), and the bill's expenses (decision 6 of 17c: a bill has expenses, so a debit
    note can take money off them). `leftToDebit` shows the money cap of 17d.1 under each line.
  - `postHint` says what posting takes off (decision 1: the goods, their price difference, the VAT input) and where
    the money goes (decision 4).
  - On its own page, `left` is "Left for later bills" in the apply dialog's summary: the payment's "Left as advance"
    would be wrong here, since nobody paid this money ahead. `refund` records the money when the supplier pays it
    back.
- **Supplier refunds** (built like `refunds`, the other way round):
  - `sources` are the two places money can come back from (`SUPPLIER_REFUND_SOURCE_TYPES`). The source box shows each
    with what is left (`sourceOption`, from `unappliedOf()`), and `amountHint` repeats the cap, so
    `supplier_refund_over_source` is rare.
  - `account` is "Received into": the money comes in, so it is the receipt's word, not the customer refund's "Paid
    from". The reference examples are money coming from a supplier: their cheque, their sales officer's cash.
  - `saveHint` says saving posts at once. The void words follow the supplier payment's; the date hint names the case
    that makes a refund void (their cheque bounced).
- **Print.** Three titles. A printed debit note shows the original bill's number and date (`originalBill`,
  `billDate`): the supplier's accountant files it against that bill. `supplierCredit` prints their Mushak 6.7 number
  when there is one. A return slip names the goods receipt of each line (`goodsReceipt`) and the warehouse it left
  from (`sentFrom`), and gets a supplier's signature line (`signatures.supplier`): the driver who takes the goods
  signs for them. A refund prints `receivedFrom` and `amountReceived` (from 15c) with `receivedInto` and `paidBackOn`.
- **Permissions.** Each text says what the person may do, in the words of the screen.
- **The audit words.** `audit.fields` gets the two field names 17d.3 writes that the log did not know: `bill` (a debit
  note's bill) and `supplierCreditNumber`. The rest (`number`, `date`, `supplier`, `warehouse`, `reason`, `lines`,
  `total`, `entry`, `applied`, `amount`, `method`, `source`, `reversal`) were there already. `debit_note.allocated`
  writes the bill numbers as field names, like `supplier_payment.allocated`.
- **Each error message says how to fix the problem** (CLAUDE.md → Copy). A few notes:
  - `purchase_return_over_received`, `debit_note_over_line`, `debit_note_over_return`, `debit_note_over_bill` and
    `supplier_refund_over_source` also cover the races of 17d.3: when another document won, the API maps the database
    check to these codes. So each says another document may have taken some first, and to reload.
  - `purchase_return_receipt_line_invalid` also answers a bill and a return of the same goods posted at the same
    moment (17d.3's `returnRace`), so it names that case and says to reload.
  - `debit_note_over_line` sits under a line's price or an expense's amount (17d.3), so it names the amount, the
    price and the quantity: the person decides which one to lower.
  - `purchase_return_cost_unknown` gives both ways out: send the goods back from their goods receipt, or bring in the
    item's opening stock so it has a cost.
  - `debit_note_line_invalid` and `debit_note_return_invalid` each cover a debit note with a bill and one without
    (decision 9), so each says what to do in both cases.
  - `payment_has_refunds` says which document to void first, like `receipt_has_refunds` of 15d.
- **Four older texts change,** because 17d makes them wrong or incomplete:
  - `purchase_not_draft`. A posted debit note answers it (17d.3), and so did a posted bill in 17c. The old text said
    "Reopen it first", which is only true for a document waiting for approval. The new one says both cases.
  - `journal_account_stock` names the purchase return and the debit note as two more documents that post to goods
    received not billed (decisions 1 and 2).
  - `payment_void_date`. A supplier refund's void reuses this code (17d.1), and the old "the day the money was paid"
    is wrong for money that came in. The new text names the payment's or the refund's own date.
  - `journal_is_purchase` now covers the two new sources: a refund is voided, and a bill is corrected with a debit
    note.

The Bangla follows the words of 15d and 17c. A few choices:

- **"পারচেজ রিটার্ন", "ডেবিট নোট", "সাপ্লায়ার রিফান্ড"**: the words a Bangladeshi accounts office uses, like
  "সেলস রিটার্ন" and "ক্রেডিট নোট" on the sales side. A plain Bangla word for a debit note would be unknown to the
  accountant who reads it.
- **"ভয়েড"** for a voided supplier refund, the word 17c chose for a voided supplier payment. The customer's refund
  says "বাতিল", but on the purchase side "বাতিল" is the cancelled status of a bill or a payment, and the two must stay
  apart.
- **"ফেরত পাঠানো"** (sent back) for the stock card's movement, next to the sales return's "ফেরত এসেছে" (came back):
  the direction is in the word.
- **"তাদের কাছে ৳… পাওনা"** for `suppliers.inAdvance`: what the supplier owes the company, whether from an advance or
  a debit note.
- **"মূসক ৬.৭"** for Mushak 6.7, the way the bill writes "মূসক ৬.৩".
- Owner, permission keys, VAT, BEFTN and bKash stay in English inside the Bangla text, as in the rest of the file
  (CLAUDE.md → Language).

### Check this part

```bash
pnpm --filter @omnivo/contracts build
pnpm --filter @omnivo/i18n typecheck
pnpm --filter @omnivo/i18n test
pnpm --filter @omnivo/i18n build
pnpm --filter @omnivo/ui typecheck
```

Build `@omnivo/contracts` first: the i18n package reads its built `ErrorCode` type, so until then the 32 new codes
are unknown and the `satisfies` line fails the other way round. Build `@omnivo/i18n` before you type-check the ui
package and the app, which read its built types.

> **What we checked in this part.** `packages/i18n` type-checks, ESLint and Prettier are clean, its unit tests pass
> (11), and it builds. `packages/ui` type-checks against the new build, and the repo's `pnpm lint` gets past the i18n
> build again. The app has 13 type errors left, all about the new fields in the bill pills, the bill test fixture and
> the mocks (17d.6, 17d.7); none is about a missing translation key. To be sure `bn.ts` cannot fall behind, we removed
> two Bangla keys on purpose, one at a time (an error text and a word in the new `purchaseReturns` section): the type
> check failed each time, and passed again with the key back.

## 17d.6 — `apps/app`: the screens, and the printed pages

This part adds the purchase returns, the debit notes and the supplier refunds: their lists, forms, pages and printed
sheets. It also changes the screens 17d's contract touches: the bill form bills only what a receipt line kept, the
bill's page shows what debit notes took off, the goods receipt's page shows what went back, the supplier payment's
page can record money paid back, and the journal and the stock card open the new documents.

When this part starts, the app has 13 type errors (17d.5 lists them). When it ends, the app's own code type-checks,
its scripts and e2e projects too; the 9 errors left are all in `src/mocks/`, which 17d.7 brings up to the new
contract. Because of them `pnpm --filter @omnivo/app build` (which runs `tsc` first) still fails, so the bundle is
checked with `vite build` directly below. Nothing here is clicked through in a browser yet: the mock API and the
Playwright tests are 17d.7.

The order below is the order to write the files in: each one only uses files above it.

- **Everything new is under `['purchase', tenantId]`,** like 17a–17c's documents. Posting a return changes its goods
  receipts (what went back), its orders (received) and its bills; posting a debit note changes its bill and its
  returns (debited); a refund changes the debit note or payment it takes money back from. One invalidate of the
  prefix (`usePurchaseRefresh`) refreshes all of them, so no screen can forget one.
- **`returnableReceiptsQuery` uses the contract's `return=returnable` filter** (17d.1): the supplier's posted receipts
  with a line that still keeps something. The return form's picker lists exactly those, so a receipt whose goods all
  went back never shows up just to say "nothing left".
- **`postedBillsQuery` and `postedPurchaseReturnsQuery` read the newest 100,** like the credit note's two pickers
  (15d). A bill older than that is reached from its own page ("Write debit note"), which starts the form with it.
- **`supplierRefundSourcesQuery` reads the supplier's posted debit notes and payments,** 100 of each, and the form
  keeps the ones with money left. Neither list can filter on "money left", and the filter lives on the form, not
  here: every list page imports this file, and the refund's helpers would ride along into each of their chunks.
- **Every document query has `retry: false`,** like every document: a deleted draft answers 404 at once, and the
  page shows "not found" instead of retrying three times.


Decision 40. Since 17d.3 the API bills a receipt line's kept quantity (accepted less what went back before the
bill) and refuses anything else (`bill_receipt_line_quantity`). The form has to start there.

- **`BillLineOrigin.returnedQuantity`** is what went back before billing, in the base unit. It is `'0'` for a saved
  draft, whose lines do not say: a draft was saved with the right quantity already, so only the hint is missing.
  15d's `LineOrigin` made the same choice for an invoice line of a challan.
- **`receiptOrderValue()` takes the returned share off.** The goods receipt booked the order's value of what was
  accepted; each return put back its share of that value (17d.3's `returnValue()`), and because returns count it over
  everything sent back so far, their values add up to exactly `prorate(value, returned, base)`. So the form's
  "order's value" is the API's `orderValue` to the paisa, and the price difference it shows is the one posting books.
  Counting the returns' own values instead would need a request per receipt line.
- **`receiptBilledQuantity()` picks the unit and the quantity.** Nothing went back: the receipt's own unit and
  quantity, "16 bag" as it came in. Something did: still the receipt's unit when what is left is a whole number of
  it (13 bags), else the base unit (660 kg is 13.2 bags). 15d's `billedUnitOf()` always moves to the base unit; a
  bill must not, because a price moved to a smaller unit is rounded to 4 decimals. ৳62 a gross is ৳0.4306 a piece, so
  500 gross billed as 72,000 pieces come to ৳31,003.20, and posting books the ৳3.20 as a price difference nobody
  agreed to. 17d.7's browser test found this.
- **What is left in the receipt's unit is worked out with `prorateMoney()`:** the receipt line's quantity × kept ÷
  its base quantity, to 4 decimals. It is a sum on two 4-decimal strings, so the money helper does it exactly;
  `decimal.js` would add a library to every bill page. The unit is used only when the result is whole and
  `toBaseQuantity()` gives back exactly what was kept, the API's own check (`bill_receipt_line_quantity`).
- **`receiptLineToBill()` bills the kept quantity in that unit,** and an amount discount goes with the kept share of
  the order line, not the accepted share: 650 kg of an order of 2,000 kg carry ৳650 of its ৳2,000 off. The price
  moves to the billed unit with the same `priceInUnit()` as before.
- **`receiptLinesLeft()` leaves out a line that kept nothing,** the same way it left out a line that accepted
  nothing (decision 43 of 17c): there is nothing on it to bill.

`purchaseReturnReasonKey()` and `debitReasonKey()` sit here, next to the sales ones, and not in the new

### The parts without React: `lib/purchase-returns.ts` (new)

The return, the debit note and the refund helpers in one file, unit-tested below, like 15d's `lib/returns.ts`. It
imports only `lib/returns.ts` and `lib/sales.ts`, both small, so the return's pages stay light.

```ts
import {
  type Bill,
  type BillExpense,
  type BillLine,
  compareMoney,
  type DebitNoteExpenseFormValues,
  type DebitNoteLine,
  type DebitNoteLineFormValues,
  type DebitNoteSummary,
  defaultLineDescription,
  type DocumentTotals,
  documentTotals,
  draftLineAmounts,
  expenseLineAmounts,
  type GoodsReceiptLine,
  isMoneyAmount,
  isZeroMoney,
  isZeroQuantity,
  keptQuantity,
  type LineAmounts,
  plainQuantity,
  prorateMoney,
  type PurchaseReturn,
  type PurchaseReturnLine,
  type PurchaseReturnLineFormValues,
  subtractMoney,
  subtractQuantity,
  type SupplierPaymentSummary,
  type SupplierRefundSourceType,
  unappliedOf,
  type VariantRef,
} from '@omnivo/contracts';

import { priceIn } from './returns';
import { formDiscount } from './sales';

// The pure parts of the purchase return, debit note and supplier refund pages (step 17d),
// unit-tested in purchase-returns.spec.ts. The sales return, credit note and refund of 15d seen
// from the buyer's side (lib/returns.ts), with a goods receipt where those have a challan and a
// bill where they have an invoice.

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Purchase returns

// The lines of a goods receipt a return may still send back: something kept (accepted less what
// posted returns sent back already), and not on the form already (a receipt line once per return:
// purchase_return_line_twice). Billed or not does not matter: a billed line goes back too, and a
// debit note takes its money off.
export function returnableReceiptLines(
  lines: readonly GoodsReceiptLine[],
  onForm: ReadonlySet<string>,
): GoodsReceiptLine[] {
  return lines.filter((line) => !isZeroQuantity(keptQuantity(line)) && !onForm.has(line.id));
}

// A receipt line as a return line, with everything that can still go back. Nothing went back yet:
// the receipt's own unit and quantity, and its serial numbers. Some did: the base unit with what is
// kept, and no serial numbers, because the line does not say which ones are still here; the store
// keeper types the numbers on the goods. The batch stays empty: the server takes the receipt
// line's own (purchase_return_batch_not_allowed otherwise).
export function receiptLineToReturn(line: GoodsReceiptLine): PurchaseReturnLineFormValues {
  const whole = isZeroQuantity(line.returnedQuantity);
  return {
    variantId: line.variantId,
    unitId: whole ? line.unitId : line.baseUnitId,
    quantity: plainQuantity(whole ? line.quantity : keptQuantity(line)),
    batchId: '',
    serialNumbers: whole ? line.serialNumbers : [],
    receiptLineId: line.id,
  };
}

// A saved draft's line as the form holds it. A receipt line names no batch (the API sent the
// receipt line's batch for the page; the contract refuses it on such a line).
export function toPurchaseReturnFormLine(line: PurchaseReturnLine): PurchaseReturnLineFormValues {
  return {
    variantId: line.variantId,
    unitId: line.unitId,
    quantity: plainQuantity(line.quantity),
    batchId: line.receiptLineId === null ? (line.batchId ?? '') : '',
    serialNumbers: line.serialNumbers,
    receiptLineId: line.receiptLineId ?? '',
  };
}

// What debit notes have not taken the money off for yet, in the base unit. Two kinds of line have
// money to take off: one a bill had billed when the return was posted, and one on its own (goods
// from before the system, a debit note without a bill, decision 9). A receipt line not billed yet
// made its bill smaller instead.
export function leftToDebitOf(
  line: Pick<
    PurchaseReturnLine,
    'receiptLineId' | 'billLineId' | 'baseQuantity' | 'debitedQuantity'
  >,
): string {
  const debitable = line.receiptLineId === null || line.billLineId !== null;
  return debitable ? subtractQuantity(line.baseQuantity, line.debitedQuantity) : '0';
}

// The return lines a debit note can still take the money off for: billed on this bill (or, for a
// debit note without a bill, `billId` null, the lines on their own), not all debited, and not on
// the form already (debit_note_return_twice)
export function debitableReturnLines(
  purchaseReturn: Pick<PurchaseReturn, 'lines'>,
  billId: string | null,
  onForm: ReadonlySet<string>,
): PurchaseReturnLine[] {
  return purchaseReturn.lines.filter(
    (line) =>
      (billId === null ? line.receiptLineId === null : line.billId === billId) &&
      !isZeroQuantity(leftToDebitOf(line)) &&
      !onForm.has(line.id),
  );
}

// Where "Write debit note" on a return starts: the first bill with goods of the return not debited
// yet, else a debit note without a bill for its lines on their own; null when nothing is left. A
// return can hold lines of two bills; a debit note is for one, so the button stays until all are
// debited.
export function debitStartOf(
  purchaseReturn: Pick<PurchaseReturn, 'lines'>,
): { billId: string | null } | null {
  const line = purchaseReturn.lines.find((item) => !isZeroQuantity(leftToDebitOf(item)));
  if (line === undefined) return null;
  return { billId: line.receiptLineId === null ? null : line.billId };
}
```

- **`returnableReceiptLines()` does not care whether a line was billed.** A billed line goes back too; a debit note
  takes its money off afterwards (decision 1). It leaves out a line that kept nothing and a line already on the
  form: a receipt line once per return (`purchase_return_line_twice`).
- **`receiptLineToReturn()` sends back everything that is left.** Nothing went back yet: the receipt's own unit,
  quantity and serial numbers, so a whole line goes back with no typing. Some did: the base unit with what is kept,
  and no serial numbers, because the line does not say which numbers are still in the store; the store keeper types
  the ones on the goods. The batch stays empty: the server takes the receipt line's own lot and refuses another
  (`purchase_return_batch_not_allowed`).
- **`toPurchaseReturnFormLine()` drops a receipt line's batch** for the same reason: the API sent the receipt line's
  lot for the page to show, and sending it back would be refused. A line on its own keeps its batch, which the store
  keeper picked.
- **`leftToDebitOf()` is what debit notes still have to take off,** and only two kinds of line have anything: one a
  bill had billed when the return was posted (`billLineId`), and one on its own (decision 9). A receipt line that was
  not billed made the bill smaller instead (decision 1), so it has nothing to debit and must not keep the "Write debit
  note" button alive.
- **`debitableReturnLines()` takes a bill id or `null`.** With a bill, the lines that bill billed; with `null` (a
  debit note without a bill), the lines on their own. These are the two kinds of debit note the API accepts.
- **`debitStartOf()`** answers where "Write debit note" on a return starts (decision 44): the bill of the first line
  with something left, `{ billId: null }` when that line is on its own, `null` when nothing is left (the page then
  shows no button). The order of the lines decides, so the result is the same every time the page opens.

```ts
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Debit notes

// What a bill line or expense can still take off: its total, less what posted debit notes took.
// The money cap of 17d.1 (debit_note_over_line).
export function debitLeft(line: Pick<BillLine | BillExpense, 'total' | 'debited'>): string {
  return subtractMoney(line.total, line.debited);
}

// What a line of a debit note shows and is worked out from: the item, its units, and the VAT rate
// when it is fixed (a bill line's), or null when the person picks it (a line on its own)
export type DebitItem = VariantRef & { units: readonly { unitId: string; factor: string }[] };

function itemOf(line: DebitItem): DebitItem {
  return {
    variantId: line.variantId,
    productId: line.productId,
    productCode: line.productCode,
    productName: line.productName,
    optionValues: line.optionValues,
    sku: line.sku,
    baseUnitId: line.baseUnitId,
    units: line.units,
  };
}

// A return line of a bill as a debit note line: the goods that went back, at the price the bill
// line charged. Nothing debited yet: the return's own unit and quantity. Some was: the base unit
// with what is left. An amount discount goes with the share of the bill line that went back, like
// returnLineToCredit() of 15d.
export function returnLineToDebit(
  returnLine: PurchaseReturnLine,
  billLine: BillLine,
): DebitNoteLineFormValues {
  const whole = isZeroQuantity(returnLine.debitedQuantity);
  const unitId = whole ? returnLine.unitId : returnLine.baseUnitId;
  const left = leftToDebitOf(returnLine);
  return {
    billLineId: billLine.id,
    returnLineId: returnLine.id,
    taxRateId: '',
    unitId,
    quantity: plainQuantity(whole ? returnLine.quantity : left),
    description:
      billLine.description === defaultLineDescription(billLine) ? '' : billLine.description,
    unitPrice: priceIn(billLine, unitId),
    discountType: billLine.discountType,
    discount: formDiscount(
      billLine.discountType === 'percent'
        ? billLine.discount
        : prorateMoney(billLine.discount, left, billLine.baseQuantity),
    ),
  };
}

// A return line on its own as a line of a debit note without a bill: what is left of it, with the
// price and the VAT rate empty. Nothing in the system says what the supplier charged for goods from
// before it, so both are typed from the supplier's credit note.
export function ownReturnLineToDebit(returnLine: PurchaseReturnLine): DebitNoteLineFormValues {
  const whole = isZeroQuantity(returnLine.debitedQuantity);
  return {
    billLineId: '',
    returnLineId: returnLine.id,
    taxRateId: '',
    unitId: whole ? returnLine.unitId : returnLine.baseUnitId,
    quantity: plainQuantity(whole ? returnLine.quantity : leftToDebitOf(returnLine)),
    description: '',
    unitPrice: '',
    discountType: 'percent',
    discount: '',
  };
}

// The item of a return line, for a line of a debit note without a bill
export function returnLineItem(line: PurchaseReturnLine): DebitItem {
  return itemOf(line);
}

// A debit note line from the API as the form holds it: the item and (with a bill) the VAT rate are
// the bill line's, so only the ids go back. A line without a bill sends its own rate.
export function toDebitFormLine(line: DebitNoteLine): DebitNoteLineFormValues {
  return {
    billLineId: line.billLineId ?? '',
    returnLineId: line.returnLineId ?? '',
    taxRateId: line.billLineId === null ? line.taxRate.id : '',
    unitId: line.unitId,
    quantity: plainQuantity(line.quantity),
    description: line.description === defaultLineDescription(line) ? '' : line.description,
    unitPrice: line.unitPrice,
    discountType: line.discountType,
    discount: formDiscount(line.discount),
  };
}

// The item of a saved line on its own (a debit note without a bill): the line carries it
export function debitLineItem(line: DebitNoteLine): DebitItem {
  return itemOf(line);
}

// A bill expense as a debit note expense, with what is left of it. Nothing debited yet: the amount
// as the bill typed it, so the whole expense comes off to the paisa. Some was: the same share of the
// typed amount as of the total, which the server checks again (debit_note_over_line); a paisa of
// rounding over is refused there, and the person lowers it.
export function expenseToDebit(expense: BillExpense): DebitNoteExpenseFormValues {
  const left = debitLeft(expense);
  return {
    billExpenseId: expense.id,
    amount: plainQuantity(
      isZeroMoney(expense.debited)
        ? expense.amount
        : prorateMoney(expense.amount, left, expense.total),
    ),
  };
}

// The bill expenses a debit note can still take money off: something left, not on the form
export function debitableExpenses(
  expenses: readonly BillExpense[],
  onForm: ReadonlySet<string>,
): BillExpense[] {
  return expenses.filter(
    (expense) => compareMoney(debitLeft(expense), '0') > 0 && !onForm.has(expense.id),
  );
}
```

- **`debitLeft()` is the money cap of 17d.1** (`debit_note_over_line`): a bill line's or expense's total less what
  posted debit notes took. The editor shows it under each line so the person sees the limit before the API says it.
- **`DebitItem` is what a line needs to be drawn:** the variant and its units. A bill line has them; a line without
  a bill has no bill line, so the form keeps the return line's item for it (`returnLineItem()`), and a saved draft's
  line carries its own (`debitLineItem()`). `itemOf()` copies only those fields, so a whole return line is not kept
  in the form's state.
- **`returnLineToDebit()` is 15d's `returnLineToCredit()`:** the goods that went back at the price the bill line
  charged, moved to the return line's unit (`priceIn()` from `lib/returns.ts`, which works on any line with a price,
  a unit and units). Nothing debited yet: the return's own unit and quantity. Some was: the base unit with what is
  left. An amount discount goes with the share that went back, so debiting all the goods of a line takes off
  exactly what the line charged.
- **`ownReturnLineToDebit()` leaves the price and the VAT rate empty.** Nothing in the system says what the supplier
  charged for goods bought before it; both come from the supplier's credit note. A guessed price would be posted by
  someone who did not look.
- **`toDebitFormLine()` sends a line without a bill back with its own rate,** and a line of a bill without one: the
  contract refuses a rate on a bill's line (`debit_note_tax_rate_not_allowed`), because the VAT taken off must be the
  VAT that was claimed.
- **`expenseToDebit()` starts with what is left of an expense.** Nothing debited: the amount as the bill typed it,
  so the whole expense comes off to the paisa. Some was: the same share of the typed amount as of the total. That
  share can round a paisa over the cap; the server checks again and the person lowers it, which is better than
  starting every partial expense a paisa short.

```ts
// The VAT rate a line is worked out at: its bill line's (the VAT taken off is the VAT that was
// claimed), or on a debit note without a bill the one picked on the line. null = not known yet.
export function debitLineRate(
  line: Pick<DebitNoteLineFormValues, 'billLineId' | 'taxRateId'>,
  billLines: ReadonlyMap<string, Pick<BillLine, 'taxRate'>>,
  rateOf: (id: string) => string | null,
): string | null {
  const billLineId = line.billLineId ?? '';
  if (billLineId !== '') return billLines.get(billLineId)?.taxRate.rate ?? null;
  const taxRateId = line.taxRateId ?? '';
  return taxRateId === '' ? null : rateOf(taxRateId);
}

// The form's totals, worked out like the API: each line at its rate, each expense at its bill
// expense's rate, all the debit note's way of writing prices. A line or an expense whose boxes are
// not complete yet counts as nothing, like the bill form's.
export function debitFormTotals(
  lines: readonly DebitNoteLineFormValues[],
  expenses: readonly DebitNoteExpenseFormValues[],
  bill: Pick<Bill, 'lines' | 'expenses'> | null,
  rateOf: (id: string) => string | null,
  pricesIncludeVat: boolean,
): DocumentTotals {
  const billLines = new Map(bill?.lines.map((line) => [line.id, line]));
  const billExpenses = new Map(bill?.expenses.map((expense) => [expense.id, expense]));
  const amounts = [
    ...lines.map((line) =>
      draftLineAmounts(
        {
          quantity: line.quantity,
          unitPrice: line.unitPrice,
          discountType: line.discountType,
          discount: line.discount,
        },
        debitLineRate(line, billLines, rateOf),
        pricesIncludeVat,
      ),
    ),
    ...expenses.map((expense) => {
      // draftExpenseAmounts() of lib/bills.ts, written out: importing it would bring the bill's
      // helpers into every purchase return page
      const source = billExpenses.get(expense.billExpenseId);
      const amount = expense.amount.trim();
      return source && isMoneyAmount(amount)
        ? expenseLineAmounts({ amount, rate: source.taxRate.rate }, pricesIncludeVat)
        : null;
    }),
  ];
  return documentTotals(amounts.filter((amount): amount is LineAmounts => amount !== null));
}
```

- **`debitLineRate()`:** a bill line's rate, or the one picked on a line without a bill; `null` until one is picked,
  so that line counts as nothing yet.
- **`debitFormTotals()` adds the lines and the expenses,** each the API's way (`draftLineAmounts()`, and
  `expenseLineAmounts()` for an expense at its bill expense's rate), all in the debit note's way of writing prices.
  A box being typed counts as nothing, like the bill form's totals. The expense half is `draftExpenseAmounts()` of
  `lib/bills.ts` written out in four lines: importing it would bring the bill's helpers into every return page.

```ts
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Supplier refunds

// A place a supplier can pay money back on: a posted debit note's or a posted payment's money that
// is not applied to a bill and not paid back yet (unappliedOf)
export interface SupplierRefundSourceOption {
  type: SupplierRefundSourceType;
  id: string;
  number: string;
  date: string;
  // Where the refund starts: the branch the money was owed at
  branchId: string;
  left: string;
}

// The supplier's posted debit notes and payments with money left, the oldest first, like
// refundSourcesOf() of 15d
export function supplierRefundSourcesOf(
  debitNotes: readonly DebitNoteSummary[],
  payments: readonly SupplierPaymentSummary[],
): SupplierRefundSourceOption[] {
  const fromDebitNotes = debitNotes.flatMap((note): SupplierRefundSourceOption[] =>
    note.status === 'posted' && note.number !== null
      ? [
          {
            type: 'debit_note',
            id: note.id,
            number: note.number,
            date: note.date,
            branchId: note.branchId,
            left: unappliedOf({
              amount: note.total,
              applied: note.applied,
              refunded: note.refunded,
            }),
          },
        ]
      : [],
  );
  const fromPayments = payments.flatMap((payment): SupplierRefundSourceOption[] =>
    payment.status === 'posted' && payment.number !== null
      ? [
          {
            type: 'supplier_payment',
            id: payment.id,
            number: payment.number,
            date: payment.date,
            branchId: payment.branchId,
            left: unappliedOf(payment),
          },
        ]
      : [],
  );
  return [...fromDebitNotes, ...fromPayments]
    .filter((source) => compareMoney(source.left, '0') > 0)
    .toSorted((a, b) => a.date.localeCompare(b.date) || a.number.localeCompare(b.number));
}

// The form's one select for two boxes: "debit_note:<id>" or "supplier_payment:<id>"
export function supplierSourceKeyOf(source: {
  type: SupplierRefundSourceType;
  id: string;
}): string {
  return `${source.type}:${source.id}`;
}

// The two boxes the API wants from the select's value ('' for none)
export function supplierSourceFields(key: string): { debitNoteId: string; paymentId: string } {
  const [type, id = ''] = key.split(':');
  return {
    debitNoteId: type === 'debit_note' ? id : '',
    paymentId: type === 'supplier_payment' ? id : '',
  };
}
```

The refund's helpers, 15d's `refundSourcesOf()`, `sourceKeyOf()` and `sourceFields()` for the supplier's side. The
sources are the supplier's posted debit notes and posted payments with money left, the oldest first: an advance or a
debit note that waited longest is usually the one paid back. A draft debit note and a voided payment hold no money,
so they are left out. The select has one value for two boxes (`debit_note:<id>`), and `supplierSourceFields()` turns
it into the two the API wants, exactly one filled (`supplier_refund_source` otherwise).

Decision 39.

- **`GoodsReceiptReturnPill` shows nothing for `none`:** nothing going back is the normal case, and a pill on every
  row would say nothing. It is neutral, like the challan's: a return is neither a success nor a problem. The
  `satisfies Record<Exclude<GrnReturnState, 'none'>, …>` makes the type check fail if the contract adds a state and
  this map does not.
- **`BillPills` reads `debitStateOf()`.** Debited in full replaces the payment pill (the bill is undone, there is
  nothing to pay); partly debited sits beside it. `billPaymentStatusOf()` and `isBillOverdue()` already count what
  debit notes applied (17d.1), so a bill settled by a debit note reads "Paid", never "Overdue".

Decision 48, and decision 7: the browser prints them, so they work offline and need no PDF service.

- **`PricedLines` gets `extra` and `returnWords`.** A debit note's total counts its expenses, so they must sit
  between the lines and the totals, inside the block that adds up; and a debit note line says "Goods sent back on
  PRN-…", where a credit note line says "Goods back on SR-…". Both are optional, so the sales documents do not change.
- **`PurchaseReturnPrint` is the goods-out slip** that travels with the goods. The first signature is the supplier's
  (their driver signs for what he takes), then whoever loaded it and whoever authorised it. Each line names the goods
  receipt it came in on: that is how the supplier finds its own challan.
- **`DebitNotePrint` names the bill twice,** our number and the supplier's own (`BILL-… · PSM/2026/0412`), because
  their accountant files it against theirs, and their credit note (Mushak 6.7) with its date when they gave one. A
  meta row that does not apply is `null`, which `Sheet` already leaves out.
- **`SupplierRefundPrint` is a voucher of money received,** the money receipt's layout: who paid, how much in figures
  and words, how, into which account, and on which debit note or payment. The page passes the account's name, as the
  payment voucher does.

### The bill's page: `components/expenses-table.tsx` (new), `components/bill-view.tsx`

```tsx
import type { Account, DocumentTotals, TaxRateRef } from '@omnivo/contracts';
import { useLocale } from '@omnivo/i18n';
import { Card, CardHeader } from '@omnivo/ui';
import type { ReactNode } from 'react';

import { useRateText } from '../lib/tax-rates';
import { SalesTotals } from './sales-parts';

// An expense as the page shows it: a bill's (17c) or a debit note's (17d), both of which carry the
// bill expense's account, description and VAT rate
interface ShownExpense {
  id: string;
  accountId: string;
  description: string;
  taxRate: TaxRateRef;
  net: string;
  total: string;
}

export const accountLabel = (account: Account | undefined) =>
  account ? `${account.code} · ${account.name}` : '—';

// The expenses, read only, with the document's totals under them: they count the item lines too.
// The bill's page had it in 17c (bill-view.tsx); step 17d moved it here for the debit note's page,
// a file of its own so that page does not load the bill's.
export function ExpensesTable<E extends ShownExpense>({
  title,
  subtitle,
  expenses,
  totals,
  pricesIncludeVat,
  accountOf,
  detail,
}: {
  title: string;
  subtitle: string;
  expenses: readonly E[];
  totals: DocumentTotals;
  pricesIncludeVat: boolean;
  accountOf: (id: string) => Account | undefined;
  // Words under an expense's description (what debit notes took off it)
  detail?: (expense: E) => ReactNode;
}) {
  const { t, format } = useLocale();
  const rateText = useRateText();
  const money = (value: string) => format.money(value, { decimals: 2 });
  return (
    <Card className="overflow-hidden">
      <CardHeader title={title} subtitle={subtitle} />
      <div className="mt-4 overflow-x-auto">
        <table className="w-full min-w-[640px] border-collapse text-body-sm">
          <caption className="sr-only">{title}</caption>
          <thead>
            <tr className="bg-subtle text-left text-caption font-medium text-ink-3">
              <th scope="col" className="px-5 py-2.5">
                {t('bills.expenseDescription')}
              </th>
              <th scope="col" className="px-5 py-2.5">
                {t('bills.expenseAccount')}
              </th>
              <th scope="col" className="px-5 py-2.5">
                {t('bills.expenseVat')}
              </th>
              <th scope="col" className="px-5 py-2.5 text-right">
                {t('salesLines.amount')}
              </th>
            </tr>
          </thead>
          <tbody>
            {expenses.map((expense) => (
              <tr key={expense.id} className="border-t border-line align-top">
                <td className="px-5 py-3 font-medium text-ink">
                  {expense.description}
                  {detail?.(expense)}
                </td>
                <td className="px-5 py-3">{accountLabel(accountOf(expense.accountId))}</td>
                <td className="px-5 py-3 whitespace-nowrap">
                  {expense.taxRate.name}
                  <span className="block text-caption text-ink-3 tabular-nums">
                    {rateText(expense.taxRate.rate)}
                  </span>
                </td>
                <td className="px-5 py-3 text-right font-medium whitespace-nowrap tabular-nums">
                  {money(pricesIncludeVat ? expense.total : expense.net)}
                </td>
              </tr>
            ))}
          </tbody>
        </table>
      </div>
      <SalesTotals totals={totals} pricesIncludeVat={pricesIncludeVat} />
    </Card>
  );
}
```

17c's `BillExpensesTable`, moved out of `bill-view.tsx` and given a title and a `detail`, so the debit note's page
can show its expenses the same way. A file of its own, not an export of `bill-view.tsx`: importing from the bill's
page would put the whole bill page into the debit note's chunk.

- **"Debited" next to "Paid"**, only when something was, and a line's or an expense's own "৳6,300 debited" under it:
  the accountant who opens the bill sees where its money went without opening each debit note.
- **"Debit notes" lists the posted ones written for it,** with a minus before each total. Drafts are not on a bill
  (the contract sends posted ones only): a draft takes nothing off yet.
- **"Debit notes to apply" lists the supplier's debit notes with money left,** like the advances above it. They are
  applied from the debit note's page, where the money is (decision 24).
- **"Debit whole bill" saves a draft and opens it** (decision 45). The lines come from `wholeBillDebit()` of the
  contracts, the function the API's tests use, so the draft takes off exactly what the bill charged. It shows only
  while `canDebitWhole()`: after a first debit note, the whole amounts would be more than is left. Its error, if
  any, shows above the buttons, because the click has no form to show it in.
- **"Write debit note" stays until the bill is debited in full,** and opens an empty form for this bill.

Decision 46. 15d did the same to the money receipt's dialogs (`money-dialogs.tsx`).

- **`BillApplyForm` takes the title, the supplier, the amount, the allocations and a `save`;** the payment and the
  debit note pass their own. The rows are `billAllocationRows(…, true)` for both: a posted debit note's amounts are in
  its bills' `amountDebited` the way a payment's are in `amountPaid`, so they count back in the same way.
- **The resolvers stay in this file** (`ALLOCATION_RESOLVERS`), picked by `document`. A resolver brings the form
  library (about 14 KB gz); built on the document's page, it would load with every payment and debit note that is
  only being read. With it here, the library loads when the dialog opens.
- **`PurchaseVoidForm` takes `words`:** the payment's and the refund's sections have the same void keys, and the
  schema is the same one (`voidSupplierRefundInputSchema` is the payment's), so only the words and the route differ.
  The "keep" button is the one word that differs in name, so it is chosen in the code.
- **Both refresh the whole purchase prefix** instead of writing the saved document into the cache: the refresh
  refetches it anyway, and one path is simpler than two.

- **"Paid back"** shows what refunds took back, only when something was.
- **"Apply money" covers the amount less what was paid back:** that money cannot also go on a bill
  (`payment_over_allocated`), and the table's "Left as advance" counts from it.
- **"Record money back" opens the refund form with this payment** (decision 47), while money is left and the person
  has `purchase.refund.manage`, its own permission.
- **"Void payment" hides while a refund stands.** The API refuses it (`payment_has_refunds`); a button that can only
  fail is worse than none, and the refund's page is where it is undone.

### Purchase returns: `purchase-return-form.tsx`, `purchase-return-view.tsx` and their routes (new)

```tsx
import {
  Calendar03Icon,
  Delete02Icon,
  PackageReceiveIcon,
  PlusSignIcon,
  UserIcon,
} from '@hugeicons/core-free-icons';
import { HugeiconsIcon } from '@hugeicons/react';
import { zodResolver } from '@hookform/resolvers/zod';
import {
  contractErrorMap,
  type GoodsReceipt,
  type GoodsReceiptLine,
  keptQuantity,
  MAX_STOCK_LINES,
  plainQuantity,
  type PurchaseReturn,
  type PurchaseReturnFormValues,
  RETURN_REASONS,
  routes,
  type StockItem,
  updatePurchaseReturnInputSchema,
} from '@omnivo/contracts';
import { useLocale } from '@omnivo/i18n';
import {
  Button,
  Card,
  Dialog,
  DialogContent,
  EmptyState,
  FormAlert,
  FormField,
  Input,
  PageHeader,
  SelectField,
  TextField,
  toast,
} from '@omnivo/ui';
import { useMutation, useQueries, useQuery, useQueryClient } from '@tanstack/react-query';
import { useNavigate } from '@tanstack/react-router';
import { lazy, Suspense, useState } from 'react';
import { Controller, type Path, useFieldArray, useForm, useWatch } from 'react-hook-form';

import { call } from '../lib/api';
import { applyApiError } from '../lib/field-errors';
import { rowPath } from '../lib/products';
import {
  receiptLineToReturn,
  returnableReceiptLines,
  toPurchaseReturnFormLine,
} from '../lib/purchase-returns';
import { goodsReceiptQuery, returnableReceiptsQuery, unitsQuery } from '../lib/queries';
import { purchaseReturnReasonKey } from '../lib/returns';
import { basePreview, fefoSplit, firstMessage, serialPath } from '../lib/stock';
import { ItemPicker } from './item-picker';
import { failureOf, LineField } from './journal-parts';
import { PurchaseBackLink, usePurchaseRefresh } from './purchase-parts';
import { PickButton, PickProblem } from './sales-parts';
import { SerialNumbersInput } from './serial-numbers-input';
import { type LineItem, StockLineRow, StockLinesHeader, toLineItem } from './stock-line-row';
import { useIsoDate, useQuantity, useTenantId, useWarehouses, warehouseLabel } from './stock-parts';

// The purchase return form (step 17d): its own chunk, loaded by routes/purchase-return.tsx. The
// sales return form of 15d seen from the other side: a stock document with a supplier, whose lines
// are the stock line rows of step 13. A line sent back from a goods receipt also names that receipt
// line; a line on its own takes stock out of a batch like any line that takes stock out.

// Both bring the popover; the delivery form says why that matters for the chunk
const PartyPicker = lazy(async () => ({
  default: (await import('./party-picker')).PartyPicker,
}));
const DatePicker = lazy(async () => ({ default: (await import('./date-input')).DatePicker }));

type FormValues = PurchaseReturnFormValues;
type LineValues = FormValues['lines'][number];

// A line on its own (goods bought before the system was used): no receipt line, a batch to pick
function ownLine(item: LineItem): LineValues {
  return {
    variantId: item.variantId,
    unitId: item.baseUnitId,
    quantity: '',
    batchId: '',
    serialNumbers: [],
    receiptLineId: '',
  };
}

function fieldNames(lines: readonly LineValues[]): Path<FormValues>[] {
  return [
    'supplierId',
    'date',
    'warehouseId',
    'reason',
    'note',
    'lines',
    ...lines.flatMap((line, index) => [
      rowPath('lines', index, 'variantId'),
      rowPath('lines', index, 'unitId'),
      rowPath('lines', index, 'quantity'),
      rowPath('lines', index, 'batchId'),
      rowPath('lines', index, 'serialNumbers'),
      rowPath('lines', index, 'receiptLineId'),
      ...line.serialNumbers.map((_, serial) => serialPath(index, serial)),
    ]),
  ];
}

// The receipt line behind a return line, with its receipt's number: what the row says under the
// item ("From GRN-2026-27-0007 · 650 kg can still go back")
interface ReceiptSource {
  number: string;
  line: GoodsReceiptLine;
}

// Writing a new return (from a goods receipt, or from nothing), or changing a draft. "Save draft"
// keeps it a draft; "Post return" saves and posts in one request: the goods leave stock at the cost
// they came in at, all or nothing.
export function PurchaseReturnForm({
  purchaseReturn,
  receipt,
  today,
}: {
  purchaseReturn: PurchaseReturn | null;
  // "Send goods back" on a goods receipt: the form starts with what can still go back on it
  receipt: GoodsReceipt | null;
  today: string;
}) {
  const { t } = useLocale();
  const navigate = useNavigate();
  const tenantId = useTenantId();
  const refresh = usePurchaseRefresh();
  const quantityText = useQuantity();
  const units = useQuery(unitsQuery(tenantId)).data ?? [];
  const [picking, setPicking] = useState<'receipts' | 'items' | null>(null);
  const [confirming, setConfirming] = useState(false);
  const [items, setItems] = useState<ReadonlyMap<string, LineItem>>(
    () =>
      new Map(
        [...(purchaseReturn?.lines ?? []), ...(receipt?.lines ?? [])].map((line) => [
          line.variantId,
          toLineItem(line),
        ]),
      ),
  );
  // The receipts the lines come from: a draft's, the one it started from, and the ones the picker
  // adds. Read through the query cache, so the rows can say what is left on each receipt line.
  const [receiptIds, setReceiptIds] = useState<readonly string[]>(() => [
    ...new Set([
      ...(purchaseReturn?.receipts.map((ref) => ref.id) ?? []),
      ...(receipt ? [receipt.id] : []),
    ]),
  ]);
  const receipts = useQueries({
    queries: receiptIds.map((id) => goodsReceiptQuery(tenantId, id)),
  });
  const sources = new Map<string, ReceiptSource>();
  for (const found of receipts) {
    for (const line of found.data?.lines ?? []) {
      sources.set(line.id, { number: found.data?.number ?? '', line });
    }
  }

  const savedSupplier = purchaseReturn?.supplier ?? receipt?.supplier ?? null;
  const { active } = useWarehouses();
  const {
    register,
    control,
    handleSubmit,
    setError,
    setValue,
    getValues,
    formState: { errors, isSubmitting },
  } = useForm({
    resolver: zodResolver(updatePurchaseReturnInputSchema, { error: contractErrorMap }),
    defaultValues: {
      supplierId: savedSupplier?.id ?? '',
      date: purchaseReturn?.date ?? today,
      // From a receipt: where the goods came in, unless they were moved since. Otherwise the only
      // warehouse, or none.
      warehouseId:
        purchaseReturn?.warehouseId ??
        receipt?.warehouseId ??
        (active?.length === 1 ? (active[0]?.id ?? '') : ''),
      // A native select always shows one: the first reason, until the store keeper picks another
      reason:
        RETURN_REASONS.find((reason) => reason === purchaseReturn?.reason) ?? RETURN_REASONS[0],
      note: purchaseReturn?.note ?? '',
      lines:
        purchaseReturn?.lines.map(toPurchaseReturnFormLine) ??
        (receipt ? returnableReceiptLines(receipt.lines, new Set()).map(receiptLineToReturn) : []),
      post: false,
      version: purchaseReturn?.version ?? 1,
    },
  });
  const { fields, append, remove, insert, replace } = useFieldArray({ control, name: 'lines' });
  const lines = useWatch({ control, name: 'lines' });
  const supplierId = useWatch({ control, name: 'supplierId' });
  const warehouseId = useWatch({ control, name: 'warehouseId' });

  const addItems = (next: readonly LineItem[]) => {
    setItems((before) => {
      const map = new Map(before);
      for (const item of next) map.set(item.variantId, toLineItem(item));
      return map;
    });
  };
```

The sales return form of 15d with a supplier and goods receipts where that has a customer and challans.

- **`PartyPicker` with `role="supplier"`,** lazy like every party box, because it brings the popover. The supplier is
  a form value: the API checks that every receipt line is this supplier's.
- **The receipts behind the lines are read through the query cache** (`useQueries`), a draft's and the one it started
  from and the ones the picker adds, so each row can say what is left on its receipt line without asking twice.
- **The warehouse starts as the receipt's:** the goods usually go back from where they came in. The hint says to pick
  another one when they were moved; the stock leaves the warehouse the return names.
- **A native select always shows a reason,** so the form starts with the first one rather than an empty value the
  schema would refuse.

```tsx
  // Another supplier: the lines from the old supplier's receipts go (the API refuses them,
  // purchase_return_receipt_line_invalid); lines on their own stay
  const changeSupplier = (next: string) => {
    setValue('supplierId', next, { shouldValidate: errors.supplierId !== undefined });
    const kept = getValues('lines').filter((line) => (line.receiptLineId ?? '') === '');
    if (kept.length !== getValues('lines').length) replace(kept);
  };

  // The picker's receipt: what can still go back on it, less what is on the form already.
  // false = the return would hold too many lines; nothing is added.
  const addReceipt = (found: GoodsReceipt): boolean => {
    const onForm = new Set(
      getValues('lines').flatMap((line) => {
        const id = line.receiptLineId ?? '';
        return id === '' ? [] : [id];
      }),
    );
    const left = returnableReceiptLines(found.lines, onForm);
    if (getValues('lines').length + left.length > MAX_STOCK_LINES) return false;
    addItems(left);
    setReceiptIds((before) => (before.includes(found.id) ? before : [...before, found.id]));
    append(left.map(receiptLineToReturn));
    return true;
  };

  // FEFO for a line on its own, like the delivery form: one line per batch, from the one that
  // expires first. A line from a receipt has its receipt line's batch, so it has no such button.
  const split = (index: number, batches: readonly { batchId: string; quantity: string }[]) => {
    const now = getValues('lines')[index];
    const item = now ? items.get(now.variantId) : undefined;
    if (!now || !item) return;
    const wanted =
      now.unitId === item.baseUnitId
        ? now.quantity.trim() === ''
          ? null
          : now.quantity.trim()
        : basePreview(item, now.unitId, now.quantity, units);
    if (wanted === null) return;
    const { picks, missing } = fefoSplit(batches, wanted);
    if (picks.length === 0) return;
    remove(index);
    insert(
      index,
      picks.map((pick) => ({ ...ownLine(item), quantity: pick.quantity, batchId: pick.batchId })),
    );
    if (missing !== '0.0000') {
      toast(t('stockLines.fefoShort', { quantity: plainQuantity(missing) }));
    }
  };

  const save = (post: boolean) =>
    handleSubmit(async ({ version, ...values }) => {
      try {
        const body = { ...values, post };
        const saved = purchaseReturn
          ? await call(routes.purchaseReturns.update, {
              params: { id: purchaseReturn.id },
              body: { ...body, version },
            })
          : await call(routes.purchaseReturns.create, { body });
        await refresh();
        toast(
          saved.status === 'posted'
            ? t('purchaseReturns.posted', { number: saved.number ?? '' })
            : t('purchaseReturns.draftSaved'),
        );
        if (!purchaseReturn) {
          void navigate({
            to: '/purchase-returns/$returnId',
            params: { returnId: saved.id },
            replace: true,
          });
        }
      } catch (error) {
        applyApiError(error, fieldNames(lines), setError);
      }
    });

  const removeDraft = useMutation({
    mutationFn: (draft: PurchaseReturn) =>
      call(routes.purchaseReturns.remove, {
        params: { id: draft.id },
        query: { version: draft.version },
      }),
    onSuccess: async () => {
      await refresh();
      toast(t('purchaseReturns.deleted'));
      void navigate({ to: '/purchase-returns' });
    },
  });

  const failure = errors.root?.server?.message ?? failureOf(removeDraft.error);
  const linesError = errors.lines?.root?.message ?? errors.lines?.message;
```

- **Another supplier removes the lines from the old supplier's receipts** and keeps lines on their own: the API
  would refuse the first (`purchase_return_receipt_line_invalid`), and the second belong to no supplier yet.
- **`addReceipt()` answers `false` when the return would hold too many lines,** and adds nothing: half a receipt on
  the form would be worse than a message.
- **`split()` is the delivery form's FEFO button for a line on its own** (decision 41): one line per batch in this
  warehouse, from the one that expires first, and a toast when the stock is short. A receipt line has its own batch
  and no such button.
- **Saving and posting are one request each.** "Post return" sends `post: true`: the stock leaves, the books are
  written and the return is numbered, all or nothing. A new return is opened on its own URL with `replace`, so Back
  does not return to an empty form.

```tsx

    <div className="grid max-w-6xl grid-cols-1 gap-5">

          <Button disabled={isSubmitting || fields.length === 0} onClick={() => void save(true)()}>
            {isSubmitting ? t('purchaseReturns.posting') : t('purchaseReturns.post')}

        {picking === 'items' && (
          <ItemPicker
            warehouseId={warehouseId}
            // An archived product's goods still on the shelf can still go back (the API's rule)
            allowArchived
```
