**COMMANDS.md** — in "Look at the data", four purchase queries of 17c learn what this step added, and four new
ones follow them. In "what the company owes each supplier", the comment becomes:

```bash
# what the company owes each supplier (posted payable lines; a negative amount is an advance paid or a debit note not used yet)
```

Replace the three bill and payment queries of 17c with these. A bill owes less by what debit notes took off, an
advance is less by what was paid back, and a receipt line can be billed only for what was kept:

```bash
# open supplier bills, the oldest due first: what is still owed after payments and debit notes, and how many days late (posted bills only)
docker compose -f infra/docker/docker-compose.yml exec db psql -U postgres -d omnivo -c "SELECT t.slug, b.number, s.name AS supplier, b.supplier_bill_number, b.due_date, b.total - b.amount_paid - b.amount_debited AS still_owed, greatest(current_date - b.due_date, 0) AS days_late FROM bills b JOIN parties s ON s.tenant_id = b.tenant_id AND s.id = b.supplier_id JOIN tenants t ON t.id = b.tenant_id WHERE b.status = 'posted' AND b.amount_paid + b.amount_debited < b.total ORDER BY t.slug, b.due_date, b.number"
# supplier advances: posted payments with money not applied to a bill or paid back, and the order they were paid against
docker compose -f infra/docker/docker-compose.yml exec db psql -U postgres -d omnivo -c "SELECT t.slug, p.number, s.name AS supplier, p.date, p.amount, p.amount - p.applied - p.refunded AS advance, o.number AS against_order FROM supplier_payments p JOIN parties s ON s.tenant_id = p.tenant_id AND s.id = p.supplier_id LEFT JOIN purchase_orders o ON o.tenant_id = p.tenant_id AND o.id = p.order_id JOIN tenants t ON t.id = p.tenant_id WHERE p.status = 'posted' AND p.applied + p.refunded < p.amount ORDER BY t.slug, p.date, p.number"
# posted goods receipt lines not billed yet, oldest first: what was kept is what the next bills should cover (base unit)
docker compose -f infra/docker/docker-compose.yml exec db psql -U postgres -d omnivo -c "SELECT t.slug, g.number, s.name AS supplier, g.date, v.sku, x.base_quantity, x.returned_quantity, x.base_quantity - x.returned_quantity AS kept FROM goods_receipt_lines x JOIN goods_receipts g ON g.tenant_id = x.tenant_id AND g.id = x.receipt_id JOIN parties s ON s.tenant_id = g.tenant_id AND s.id = g.supplier_id JOIN product_variants v ON v.tenant_id = x.tenant_id AND v.id = x.variant_id JOIN tenants t ON t.id = x.tenant_id WHERE g.status = 'posted' AND NOT x.billed AND x.base_quantity > x.returned_quantity ORDER BY t.slug, g.date, g.number, x.line_no"
```

After the last purchase query, add:

```bash
# debit notes with money not yet applied to a bill or paid back (what the supplier owes the company)
docker compose -f infra/docker/docker-compose.yml exec db psql -U postgres -d omnivo -c "SELECT t.slug, d.number, s.name AS supplier, d.date, b.number AS bill, d.total - d.applied - d.refunded AS unapplied FROM debit_notes d JOIN parties s ON s.tenant_id = d.tenant_id AND s.id = d.supplier_id LEFT JOIN bills b ON b.tenant_id = d.tenant_id AND b.id = d.bill_id JOIN tenants t ON t.id = d.tenant_id WHERE d.status = 'posted' AND d.applied + d.refunded < d.total ORDER BY t.slug, d.date, d.number"
# goods sent back that no debit note has taken the money off yet (billed lines, and lines from before Omnivo)
docker compose -f infra/docker/docker-compose.yml exec db psql -U postgres -d omnivo -c "SELECT t.slug, r.number, s.name AS supplier, r.date, v.sku, l.base_quantity - l.debited_quantity AS not_debited, b.number AS bill FROM purchase_return_lines l JOIN purchase_returns r ON r.tenant_id = l.tenant_id AND r.id = l.return_id JOIN parties s ON s.tenant_id = r.tenant_id AND s.id = r.supplier_id JOIN product_variants v ON v.tenant_id = l.tenant_id AND v.id = l.variant_id LEFT JOIN bills b ON b.tenant_id = l.tenant_id AND b.id = l.bill_id JOIN tenants t ON t.id = l.tenant_id WHERE r.status = 'posted' AND (l.bill_id IS NOT NULL OR l.receipt_line_id IS NULL) AND l.debited_quantity < l.base_quantity ORDER BY t.slug, r.date, r.number, l.line_no"
# goods receipt lines whose "returned" differs from their posted returns (should print nothing)
docker compose -f infra/docker/docker-compose.yml exec db psql -U postgres -d omnivo -c "SELECT t.slug, g.number, x.line_no, x.returned_quantity, coalesce(sum(l.base_quantity) FILTER (WHERE r.status = 'posted'), 0) AS posted_returns FROM goods_receipt_lines x JOIN goods_receipts g ON g.tenant_id = x.tenant_id AND g.id = x.receipt_id JOIN tenants t ON t.id = x.tenant_id LEFT JOIN purchase_return_lines l ON l.tenant_id = x.tenant_id AND l.receipt_line_id = x.id LEFT JOIN purchase_returns r ON r.tenant_id = l.tenant_id AND r.id = l.return_id GROUP BY t.slug, g.number, x.id, x.line_no, x.returned_quantity HAVING x.returned_quantity <> coalesce(sum(l.base_quantity) FILTER (WHERE r.status = 'posted'), 0)"
# posted purchase returns, debit notes and supplier refunds with money but no journal entry (should print nothing)
docker compose -f infra/docker/docker-compose.yml exec db psql -U postgres -d omnivo -c "SELECT t.slug, x.source, x.number FROM (SELECT r.tenant_id, r.id, r.number, 'purchase_return' AS source FROM purchase_returns r WHERE r.status = 'posted' AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM purchase_return_lines l WHERE l.tenant_id = r.tenant_id AND l.return_id = r.id AND l.value > 0) UNION ALL SELECT tenant_id, id, number, 'purchase_debit_note' FROM debit_notes WHERE status = 'posted' AND total > 0 UNION ALL SELECT tenant_id, id, number, 'purchase_refund' FROM supplier_refunds) x JOIN tenants t ON t.id = x.tenant_id WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM journal_entries e WHERE e.tenant_id = x.tenant_id AND e.source = x.source AND e.document_id = x.id)"
```

The seven queries were run against a database migrated to 0042, holding 17d.2's check data. That data is written
with SQL, not through the API, so it has no journal entries, and the last query lists its posted documents; on a
database the API wrote, it prints nothing. The second and the fifth printed nothing on it, as they should (no
payment there is posted; every billed return line is debited in full), and with their filters loosened they printed
the rows they skip.

## 17d.10 — Run it

```bash
pnpm install                                  # nothing new, but run it after pulling
pnpm db:migrate                               # 0041 + 0042: seven tables, six columns, their rules
pnpm gen:openapi                              # commit it
pnpm dev                                      # restart it: 17 new routes
```

In `pnpm db:psql`:

```sql
SELECT relname, relforcerowsecurity FROM pg_class
 WHERE relname IN ('purchase_returns', 'purchase_return_lines', 'debit_notes', 'debit_note_lines',
                   'debit_note_expenses', 'debit_note_allocations', 'supplier_refunds');
                                                     -- t, seven rows
SELECT key FROM permissions
 WHERE key IN ('purchase.return.manage', 'purchase.debit_note.manage', 'purchase.refund.manage');  -- three rows
```

### What you will see

Sign in as the Owner first. (In an existing workspace the other roles do not have the new permissions yet: tick
`purchase.return.manage` for the store keeper, and the other two for the accountant, on the Roles page.)

1. **The navigation** has Purchase returns, Debit notes and Supplier refunds in the Purchase group, after Supplier
   payments.
2. **A return before the bill:** open a posted goods receipt that no bill has billed yet and click **Send goods
   back**. The form starts with every line the receipt still keeps, with "From GRN-…" and "… can still go back"
   under each. Keep one line, lower its quantity, pick a reason (Damaged) and **Post return**: it gets
   `PRN-2026-27-0001`. The receipt shows "Partly returned" and the return under "Returns"; the order goes back from
   "Received" to "Partly received"; the stock card shows the goods leaving at the receipt's cost; the journal entry is
   Dr Goods received not billed / Cr Inventory.
3. **The bill bills the rest:** **Make bill** on that receipt. The line says "… went back before billing: this bills
   the rest", and with the receipt's price no price difference notice shows.
4. **A return after the bill:** send goods back from a receipt that a posted bill billed. The return's lines say
   "Billed on BILL-…", and the page offers **Write debit note**.
5. **The debit note:** Write debit note opens the form with the bill and the returned goods at the bill's price.
   Type the supplier's credit note number (Mushak 6.7) and **Post debit note**: `DN-2026-27-0001`. The bill shows
   "Partly debited", lists the debit note and owes less; the journal entry is Dr Accounts payable / Cr Goods
   received not billed / Cr VAT input (and a Purchase price difference line when the bill's price was not the
   receipt's).
6. **Debit whole bill** on another posted bill saves a draft with every line and expense and opens it. Post it: the
   bill says "Debited". If the bill was paid, the debit note's money stays as "Left for later bills", and a newer
   bill of that supplier offers it next to the advances.
7. **Supplier refunds:** on that debit note (or a supplier payment with an advance), **Record money back**: pick a
   bank account and post it (`SRF-2026-27-0001`). The payment's page no longer shows "Void payment" while the
   refund stands. **Void** the refund with a date and a reason: the money is back on its source.
8. **Goods from before Omnivo:** New purchase return, no receipt: add a line on its own (it leaves at the average
   cost). Write debit note on it gives a debit note with no bill: type the price and VAT rate from the supplier's
   credit note, and pick the branch.
9. **Print** on a posted return, debit note and refund gives the goods-out slip, the debit note and the voucher.
10. **The store keeper** (a member with the template's permissions) sends goods back but has no Write debit note;
    the accountant writes debit notes and refunds but no returns.
11. **Bangla** and **390px**: the return lines, the debit note lines and expenses, and the allocation table fit, and
    no page scrolls sideways.

## What we found on the way

All of these are fixed in the guide — if you get stuck at the same place, you will recognise it:

- **17b's database checks needed two changes** (17d.2): they expected an order's received quantity never to go
  down, and a Received order never to go back to Approved. A return before the bill does both, on purpose
  (decision 3). Only the checks changed.
- **A debit note could not post to Goods received not billed** (17d.3): only stock documents, a bill, a reversal and
  the year-end close may post to the stock accounts. The journal's posting now lets the debit note in; a manual
  entry still may not. Found by reading, before any test ran.
- **The race test waited for the wrong lock** (17d.4): counting every session that waited on a lock picked up the
  worker's own advisory lock, so the test was flaky. It counts only waits in queries on the table it means now.
- **The race test could not know who goes first** (17d.8): it held the receipt line's lock and expected the bill,
  queued first, to post first. But both requests already hold a weak lock on that line (the foreign key check of
  their own lines), and Postgres lets such a transaction skip the row's queue, so either could win: the test failed
  once in the full run and 3 times in 6 alone. The code was right both ways (the loser sees the winner). The test
  holds the journal's number counter now, which the bill reaches only after it has the receipt line: 8 runs in 8
  pass, and a return that does not lock the line still fails it.
- **Four older texts said the wrong thing after 17d** (17d.5): `purchase_not_draft`, `journal_account_stock`,
  `payment_void_date` and `journal_is_purchase` named only the documents of 17c. And a supplier with a negative
  balance now reads "They owe you ৳…": it is no longer only an advance.
- **Five words of 17d.5 were never used** (17d.6), so they were removed from `en.ts` and `bn.ts`.
- **Pages this step never touched went over 100 KB** (17d.6): the team and units pages load the contracts' whole
  route table, which grew with the three documents. The lazy chunk budget is 105 KB (decision 49, your choice).
- **A bill after a return booked a false price difference** (17d.7): the first bill form moved every line with a
  return before it to the base unit, and the base unit's price is rounded (৳62 a gross is ৳0.4306 a piece), so 500
  gross came to ৳3.20 more than the order. The browser test found it; the line stays in the receipt's unit when it
  can (decision 40).
- **15d's refunds test found two links** (17d.7): "Supplier refunds" also matches "Refunds". The test names the link
  exactly now.
- **The role templates had none of the three permissions** (17d.8): nothing failed, but a new workspace would have
  given nobody but the owner the right to send goods back (decision 50).

---

## Notes left for later steps

**Step 18 onward:**

- **The same rounding is in 15d's invoices.** `billedUnitOf()` in `apps/app/src/lib/invoices.ts` moves a challan
  line with a return before its invoice to the base unit, like the bill form did before decision 40. The harm is
  smaller (the revenue is off by paisa, and there is no price difference account), but the fix is the same as
  `receiptBilledQuantity()`: keep the challan's unit when what was kept is a whole number of it. It was not changed
  here, because it is 15d's code.
- **The route table.** Almost every page loads the contracts' whole route table (decision 49). Loading each module's
  routes with its own pages brings the lazy budget back to 100 KB; do it before the next module's documents.
- **Landed cost and VDS** (17's decisions): a return of goods with landed cost will need the landed share back off
  the stock, and a debit note of a bill with VAT deducted at source will need the VDS share. Both start from
  `PurchaseBooksService.debitNote()`.
- **The supplier's statement** (the reports step) can read every movement of the payable from the journal: bills,
  payments, debit notes and refunds all post to it with the supplier named.

**Notes for any step:**

- **A module's role-template permissions are part of its step** (15c.8, 15d.8, 17d.8). Check
  `apps/api/src/setup/templates.ts` whenever a step adds a permission.
- **A document that posts to a stock account** (Goods received not billed, Inventory) and is not a stock source
  must be named in the `allowStock` condition of `PostingService` (`journal/posting.service.ts`, 17d.3), or its
  posting fails at runtime with `journal_account_stock`, which no type check catches.
